verses.1:1: Now there was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
verses.1:2: He had two wives: the name of one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
verses.1:3: Now that man used to go up from his town from year to year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts in Shiloh; and there the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
verses.1:4: When the day came and Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
verses.1:5: Yet to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved Hannah, even though the LORD had shut her womb.
verses.1:6: And her rival would provoke her harshly in order to distress her, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
verses.1:7: And he would do so year after year; as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, so her rival would provoke her, and she wept and would not eat.
verses.1:8: And her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah, why are you weeping? And why are you not eating? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
verses.1:9: Then Hannah stood up after eating in Shiloh and after drinking. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
verses.1:10: She was bitter in soul, and she prayed to the LORD and wept profusely.
verses.1:11: And she vowed a vow and said, "LORD of hosts, if You will truly look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, and not forget Your maidservant, but give to Your maidservant male offspring, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head."
verses.1:12: And it happened that as she kept on praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth.
verses.1:13: Now Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips were moving, and her voice could not be heard. So Eli considered her to be drunk.
verses.1:14: And Eli said to her, "How long will you stay drunk? Remove your wine from yourself."
verses.1:15: Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord. I am a woman hard-pressed in spirit, and I have not drunk wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
verses.1:16: Do not count your maidservant as a daughter of worthlessness, for out of the abundance of my complaint and my vexation I have spoken until now."
verses.1:17: And Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your request that you have asked from Him."
verses.1:18: And she said, "May your female servant find favor in your eyes." Then the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer downcast.
verses.1:19: In the morning they got up early and worshiped before the LORD; then they returned and came to their home in Ramah. And Elkanah knew his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.
verses.1:20: And it happened in the course of time that Hannah conceived and bore a son; and she called his name Samuel, "Because I have asked for him from the LORD."
verses.1:21: And the man Elkanah and all his household went up to offer to the LORD the annual sacrifice and his vow.
verses.1:22: But Hannah did not go up, because she said to her husband, "Not until the boy is weaned; then I will bring him, so that he may appear before the LORD and remain there forever."
verses.1:23: And her husband Elkanah said to her, "Do what is good in your eyes. Stay until you have weaned him; only may the LORD uphold His word." So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
verses.1:24: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with three bulls, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh; and the boy was still young.
verses.1:25: And they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
verses.1:26: And she said, "Please, my lord! As your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood beside you here to pray to the LORD.
verses.1:27: For this boy I prayed, and the LORD has given me my request that I asked from Him.
verses.1:28: And I also have lent him to the LORD; all the days that he lives, he is lent to the LORD." And there he worshiped the LORD.
verses.2:1: And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is raised high in the LORD. My mouth opens wide against my enemies, for I am glad in Your salvation.
verses.2:2: No one is holy like the LORD, for there is none apart from You, and there is no rock like our God.
verses.2:3: Do not keep speaking so very proudly, nor let insolence come forth from your mouth; for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by Him deeds are weighed.
verses.2:4: The bows of mighty men are shattered, while those who stumble gird themselves with strength.
verses.2:5: Those who were sated hire themselves out for bread, while the hungry have ceased from hunger. Even the barren woman has borne seven, while she who has many sons grows faint.
verses.2:6: The LORD puts to death and makes alive; He brings down to Sheol and brings up.
verses.2:7: The LORD impoverishes and enriches; He brings low, and He also lifts high.
verses.2:8: He raises the lowly from the dust; from the ash heap He lifts up the needy, to seat them with nobles and have them inherit a throne of honor. For the pillars of the earth belong to the LORD, and upon them He has set the world.
verses.2:9: He guards the feet of His faithful ones, while the wicked are put to silence in darkness; for not by strength does a man prevail.
verses.2:10: Those who strive against the LORD will be shattered; in the heavens He will thunder against them. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth, and He will give might to His king and raise high the horn of His anointed."
verses.2:11: Then Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house, while the boy was ministering to the LORD before Eli the priest.
verses.2:12: Now the sons of Eli were sons of worthlessness; they did not know the LORD.
verses.2:13: And this was the practice of the priests with the people: whenever any man offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand.
verses.2:14: He would thrust it into the basin, or the kettle, or the cauldron, or the pot; everything that the fork brought up, the priest would take with it. This is what they would do to all Israel who came there in Shiloh.
verses.2:15: Even before they burned the fat, the priest's servant would come and say to the man offering the sacrifice, "Give meat to roast for the priest, for he will not take boiled meat from you, but only raw."
verses.2:16: And if the man said to him, "Let them surely burn the fat first, and then take for yourself whatever your soul desires," he would reply, "No, you shall give it right now; and if not, I will take it by force."
verses.2:17: So the sin of the young men was exceedingly great in the presence of the LORD, because the men spurned the offering of the LORD.
verses.2:18: Meanwhile Samuel was ministering in the presence of the LORD, a boy girded with a linen ephod.
verses.2:19: And his mother would make a small robe for him and bring it up to him from year to year, whenever she went up with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
verses.2:20: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May the LORD grant you offspring by this woman in place of the request that was asked for the LORD." Then they would go to his home.
verses.2:21: For the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up with the LORD.
verses.2:22: Now Eli was very old, and he kept hearing everything that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they were lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.2:23: And he said to them, "Why are you doing things like these? For I keep hearing of your evil deeds from all these people.
verses.2:24: No, my sons! For the report that I hear is not good; the people of the LORD are passing it around.
verses.2:25: If a man sins against another man, God will arbitrate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?" Yet they would not listen to their father's voice, because the LORD was pleased to put them to death.
verses.2:26: Now the boy Samuel kept growing and gaining favor both with the LORD and with people.
verses.2:27: Then a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Did I not clearly reveal Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt, subject to Pharaoh's house?
verses.2:28: And did I not choose him from all the tribes of Israel to be My priest, to go up to My altar, to burn incense, and to bear an ephod before Me? And I gave to your father's house all the fire offerings of the sons of Israel.
verses.2:29: Why do you kick at My sacrifice and My offering that I commanded in My dwelling, and honor your sons more than Me, by fattening yourselves on the choicest of every offering of Israel, My people?
verses.2:30: Therefore, declares the LORD, the God of Israel, I did indeed say, 'Your house and your father's house will walk before Me forever,' yet now, declares the LORD, far be it from Me! For those who honor Me I will honor, while those who despise Me will be held in low esteem.
verses.2:31: Look, days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father's house, so that there will be no old man in your house.
verses.2:32: And you will look upon distress in My dwelling, amid all the good that will be done for Israel; and there will not be an old man in your house for all time.
verses.2:33: Yet one man of yours I will not cut off from My altar, to wear out your eyes and to make your soul languish; and all the increase of your house will die in manhood.
verses.2:34: And this will be the sign for you, what will come upon your two sons, upon Hophni and Phinehas: on a single day both of them will die.
verses.2:35: And I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest; according to what is in My heart and in My soul he will act. And I will build a sure house for him, and he will walk before My anointed for all time.
verses.2:36: And it will happen that everyone who remains in your house will come to bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, 'Please attach me to one of the priestly offices, so that I may eat a morsel of bread.'"
verses.3:1: Now the boy Samuel was serving the LORD before Eli. The word of the LORD was rare in those days, and no vision was widespread.
verses.3:2: It happened on that day that Eli was lying down in his place. His eyes had begun to grow dim, and he could not see.
verses.3:3: The lamp of God had not yet burned out, and Samuel was lying down inside the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.
verses.3:4: Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, because you called me." But he said, "I did not call; go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.
verses.3:6: Then the LORD called once more, "Samuel!" And Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, because you called me." But he said, "I did not call, my son; go back and lie down."
verses.3:7: Now Samuel did not know the LORD yet, and the word of the LORD had not been revealed to him yet.
verses.3:8: Then the LORD called Samuel again, a third time. He got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, because you called me." Then Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.
verses.3:9: Eli said to Samuel, "Go and lie down; if He calls to you, you are to say, 'Speak, LORD, because Your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
verses.3:10: Then the LORD came and took His stand, and He called as at the previous times, "Samuel! Samuel!" Samuel said, "Speak, because Your servant is listening."
verses.3:11: The LORD said to Samuel, "Look, I am about to do something in Israel such that for everyone who hears it, both of his ears will ring.
verses.3:12: On that day I will bring about against Eli everything that I have spoken about his house, from start to finish.
verses.3:13: And I declare to him that I am judging his house forever for the iniquity he knew of, because his sons were calling a curse upon themselves, and he did not restrain them.
verses.3:14: And therefore I have sworn to Eli's house that the iniquity of Eli's house will not be atoned for with sacrifice or grain offering forever."
verses.3:15: Samuel lay down until the morning and opened the doors of the house of the LORD. But Samuel was afraid to tell Eli the vision.
verses.3:16: Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son." He replied, "Here I am."
verses.3:17: He said, "What is the word He spoke to you? Please do not conceal it from me. May God do so to you, and may He add even more, if you conceal from me a single thing from the entire word He spoke to you."
verses.3:18: So Samuel told him all the words and concealed nothing from him. And he said, "It is the LORD; may He do what is good in His eyes."
verses.3:19: Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him, and He did not let any of his words fall to the ground.
verses.3:20: So all Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, came to know that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
verses.3:21: And the LORD continued to appear in Shiloh, because the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel in Shiloh through the word of the LORD.
verses.4:1: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Israel went out to face the Philistines for battle; they encamped by Ebenezer, while the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
verses.4:2: The Philistines drew up in formation to meet Israel, and the battle spread out. Israel was defeated before the Philistines, and they struck down about four thousand men in the battle line in the field.
verses.4:3: The people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, "Why has the LORD defeated us before the Philistines today? Let us take the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh to ourselves, so that it may come into our midst and save us from the grasp of our enemies."
verses.4:4: The people sent to Shiloh and carried from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who sits enthroned above the cherubim. And there with the ark of the covenant of God were Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:5: It happened when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp that all Israel shouted a great shout, and the earth reverberated.
verses.4:6: The Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said, "What is the sound of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
verses.4:7: So the Philistines were afraid, because they said, "God has come into the camp!" And they said, "Woe to us, for nothing like this has occurred before now.
verses.4:8: Woe to us! Who will rescue us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.
verses.4:9: Strengthen yourselves and be men, Philistines, or else you will serve the Hebrews just as they served you. Be men and fight!"
verses.4:10: Then the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and they fled, each man to his tent. The slaughter was very great, and thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
verses.4:11: And the ark of God was captured, and the two sons of Eli died—Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:12: Then a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, with his garments torn and earth on his head.
verses.4:13: When he came, there was Eli sitting on the seat beside the road, keeping watch, because his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And the man came to report in the city, and the entire city cried out.
verses.4:14: Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, "What is the sound of this tumult?" Then the man hurried and came and reported to Eli.
verses.4:15: Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed, and he was unable to see.
verses.4:16: The man said to Eli, "I am the one who came from the battle line, and I myself fled from the battle line today." And he said, "What has happened, my son?"
verses.4:17: The bearer of the news answered and said, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great defeat among the people. Also, your two sons have died—Hophni and Phinehas—and the ark of God has been captured."
verses.4:18: It happened when he mentioned the ark of God that he fell backward off the seat by the side of the gate; his neck was broken and he died, because the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.
verses.4:19: Now his daughter-in-law, Phinehas's wife, was pregnant and ready to give birth. When she heard the report concerning the capture of the ark of God and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she crouched down and gave birth, because her labor pains came over her.
verses.4:20: Around the time of her death, the women standing beside her spoke: "Do not be afraid, because you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer, nor did she take it to heart.
verses.4:21: And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, "Glory has gone into exile from Israel," because of the capture of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
verses.4:22: She said, "Glory has gone into exile from Israel, because the ark of God has been captured."
verses.5:1: Now the Philistines had captured the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
verses.5:2: The Philistines took the ark of God, brought it into the house of Dagon, and placed it beside Dagon.
verses.5:3: When the Ashdodites got up early the next day, there was Dagon, fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.
verses.5:4: When they got up early in the morning the next day, there was Dagon, fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD, while the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only Dagon was left on him.
verses.5:5: For this reason the priests of Dagon and all who enter the house of Dagon do not step upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod until this day.
verses.5:6: Then the hand of the LORD was heavy upon the Ashdodites; He devastated them and struck them with tumors—Ashdod and its territories.
verses.5:7: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us, because His hand is harsh against us and against Dagon our god."
verses.5:8: So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines to themselves and said, "What are we to do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And they said, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be transferred to Gath." So they transferred the ark of the God of Israel.
verses.5:9: And it came about after they had transferred it that the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumors broke out on them.
verses.5:10: So they sent the ark of God away to Ekron. And it happened when the ark of God came to Ekron that the Ekronites cried out, saying, "They have transferred the ark of the God of Israel to me, to put me and my people to death!"
verses.5:11: Then they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines and said, "Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it return to its place, so that it does not put me and my people to death." For a deadly panic was throughout the entire city; the hand of God was exceedingly heavy there.
verses.5:12: And the men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the outcry of the city rose up to heaven.
verses.6:1: Now the ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines for seven months.
verses.6:2: And the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Let us know with what we should send it to its place."
verses.6:3: And they said, "If you are sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty-handed, but you must certainly return a guilt offering to Him. Then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why His hand does not turn away from you."
verses.6:4: Then they said, "What is the guilt offering that we should return to Him?" And they said, "According to the number of the lords of the Philistines: five golden tumors and five golden mice, for one plague was on all of them and on your lords.
verses.6:5: So you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are ravaging the land, and give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps He will lighten His hand from upon you, and from upon your gods, and from upon your land.
verses.6:6: Why then should you harden your hearts, as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? After He had dealt ruthlessly with them, did they not send them away, and they departed?
verses.6:7: Now then, make one new cart and take two nursing cows on which no yoke has come, and hitch the cows to the cart, and bring their calves back home from following them.
verses.6:8: Then take the ark of the LORD and place it on the cart, and put the golden articles that you are returning to Him as a guilt offering in a box at its side; then send it away, and let it go.
verses.6:9: And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory toward Beth-shemesh, then it is He who has done this great harm to us; but if not, then we will know that it was not His hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance."
verses.6:10: So the men did so: they took two nursing cows and hitched them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
verses.6:11: And they placed the ark of the LORD on the cart, and the box, and the golden mice, and the images of their tumors.
verses.6:12: And the cows went straight along the way toward the road to Beth-shemesh; they kept going on one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines walked after them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
verses.6:13: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
verses.6:14: And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite and stopped there, where there was a large stone. Then they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.6:15: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the golden articles, and placed them on the large stone; and the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and made sacrifices on that day to the LORD.
verses.6:16: And the five lords of the Philistines saw it, and returned to Ekron on that day.
verses.6:17: Now these are the golden tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.
verses.6:18: And the golden mice were according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, from fortified city to unwalled village, and as far as Great Abel, on which they set down the ark of the LORD, which is to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.
verses.6:19: And He struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had looked into the ark of the LORD; He struck down among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men. And the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.
verses.6:20: Then the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom will He go up away from us?"
verses.6:21: So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and bring it up to you."
verses.7:1: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came, brought up the ark of the LORD, and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the LORD.
verses.7:2: From the day the ark stayed in Kiriath-jearim, the days grew many and became twenty years, and the whole house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
verses.7:3: Then Samuel spoke to the whole house of Israel, saying, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods from among you and the Ashtaroth, and set your heart firmly toward the LORD and serve Him alone; and He will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:4: So the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD alone.
verses.7:5: Then Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray on your behalf to the LORD."
verses.7:6: So they gathered together to Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day; and they said there, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.7:7: When the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered themselves to Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the sons of Israel heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
verses.7:8: And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, so that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:9: Then Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to the LORD; and Samuel cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him.
verses.7:10: Now while Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great sound on that day against the Philistines and threw them into panic, and they were defeated before Israel.
verses.7:11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
verses.7:12: Then Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer; and he said, "Up to now the LORD has helped us."
verses.7:13: So the Philistines were subdued, and they did not come into the territory of Israel again; and the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
verses.7:14: And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel returned to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and Israel rescued their territory from the hand of the Philistines. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.7:15: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
verses.7:16: And he would go from year to year, making a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and would judge Israel in all these places.
verses.7:17: Then his return was to Ramah, because his home was there, and there he judged Israel; and he built an altar to the LORD there.
verses.8:1: Now when Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.
verses.8:2: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
verses.8:3: Yet his sons did not walk in his ways, but turned aside after dishonest gain; they took bribes and perverted justice.
verses.8:4: Then all the elders of Israel assembled together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
verses.8:5: And they said to him, "Look, you have grown old, and your sons have not walked in your ways. Now appoint a king for us to judge us, like all the nations."
verses.8:6: But the matter was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
verses.8:7: And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in everything they say to you; for it is not you they have rejected, but Me they have rejected from reigning over them.
verses.8:8: According to all the deeds they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you as well.
verses.8:9: Now therefore, listen to their voice; however, you must solemnly warn them and declare to them the practice of the king who will reign over them."
verses.8:10: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
verses.8:11: And he said, "This will be the practice of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and place them for himself with his chariots and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots.
verses.8:12: And he will appoint them for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to do his plowing and to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariots.
verses.8:13: He will also take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
verses.8:14: And he will take the finest of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, and give them to his servants.
verses.8:15: He will take a tenth of your grain and your vineyards and give it to his officials and to his servants.
verses.8:16: He will also take your male servants and your female servants, and your finest young men and your donkeys, and put them to his work.
verses.8:17: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will be servants to him.
verses.8:18: And on that day you will cry out because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, yet the LORD will not answer you on that day."
verses.8:19: Yet the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, "No! Rather, there shall be a king over us,
verses.8:20: and we too will be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."
verses.8:21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and spoke them in the ears of the LORD.
verses.8:22: And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice and make a king for them." So Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, each man to his city."
verses.9:1: There was a man from Benjamin, and his name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjaminite man, a mighty man of wealth.
verses.9:2: And he had a son, and his name was Saul, a choice young man and handsome; there was not a man among the sons of Israel more handsome than he. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than all the people.
verses.9:3: Now the female donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, became lost. So Kish said to his son Saul, "Please take one of the attendants with you, get up, go, and search for the female donkeys."
verses.9:4: He passed through the hill country of Ephraim and passed through the land of Shalishah, yet they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and they were not there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjaminites, yet they did not find them.
verses.9:5: When they came to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his attendant who was with him, "Come, let us go back, or else my father will stop caring about the female donkeys and become anxious about us."
verses.9:6: He said to him, "Look now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is held in honor; everything that he speaks surely comes to pass. Now let us go there; perhaps he will tell us about our journey on which we have gone."
verses.9:7: Then Saul said to his attendant, "Look, if we go, what shall we bring to the man? For the bread is gone from our packs, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What do we have with us?"
verses.9:8: The attendant answered Saul again and said, "Look, a quarter of a shekel of silver is found in my hand; I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
verses.9:9: Formerly in Israel, this is what a man would say when going to inquire of God: "Come, let us go to the seer," for today's prophet was formerly called the seer.
verses.9:10: Then Saul said to his attendant, "Your word is good; come, let us go." So they went to the city where the man of God was.
verses.9:11: As they were going up the ascent of the city, they came upon young women going out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
verses.9:12: They answered them and said, "He is; look, he is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for he has come to the city today, because the people have a sacrifice today at the high place.
verses.9:13: As soon as you enter the city, right then you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat, for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice; afterward those who are invited will eat. Now go up, for at this very time you will find him."
verses.9:14: So they went up to the city. As they were coming into the midst of the city, there was Samuel coming out toward them to go up to the high place.
verses.9:15: Now the LORD had uncovered Samuel's ear one day before Saul came, saying,
verses.9:16: "About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over My people Israel; and he will save My people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have seen My people, because their outcry has come to Me."
verses.9:17: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD answered him, "Here is the man of whom I spoke to you! This one will govern My people."
verses.9:18: Then Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, "Please tell me where the seer's house is."
verses.9:19: Samuel answered Saul and said, "I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the high place, and you will eat with me today; in the morning I will send you off, and I will tell you everything that is in your heart.
verses.9:20: As for your female donkeys that became lost three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And for whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not for you and for all your father's house?"
verses.9:21: Saul answered and said, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribes of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me in this manner?"
verses.9:22: Then Samuel took Saul and his attendant and brought them into the hall, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited, who were about thirty men.
verses.9:23: Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion that I gave to you, about which I said to you, 'Set it aside with you.'"
verses.9:24: So the cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it and set it before Saul. And he said, "Look, what was reserved is set before you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for the appointed time, since I said, 'I have invited the people.'" So Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
verses.9:25: Then they went down from the high place into the city, and he spoke with Saul on the roof.
verses.9:26: They rose early, and at the rising of dawn Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, saying, "Get up, so that I may send you off." So Saul got up, and both of them, he and Samuel, went outside.
verses.9:27: As they were going down at the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the attendant to pass on ahead of us"—and he passed on—"but you, stand still right now, so that I may let you hear the word of God."
verses.10:1: Then Samuel took the flask of oil, poured it on his head, kissed him, and said, "Has not the LORD anointed you as ruler over His inheritance?
verses.10:2: When you leave me today, you will find two men near Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah, and they will say to you, 'The female donkeys that you went to search for have been found, and look, your father has left off the matter of the female donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'
verses.10:3: Then you will pass on farther from there and come as far as the oak of Tabor, and three men going up to God at Bethel will find you there: one carrying three young goats, and one carrying three loaves of bread, and one carrying a jar of wine.
verses.10:4: They will ask about your welfare and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall take from their hand.
verses.10:5: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the garrisons of the Philistines are; and when you arrive at the city there, you will encounter a band of prophets coming down from the high place, with a harp, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre ahead of them, and they will be prophesying.
verses.10:6: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.
verses.10:7: And when these signs come to you, do for yourself whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.
verses.10:8: And you shall go down ahead of me to Gilgal; and look, I will go down to you to offer up burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you and make known to you what you shall do."
verses.10:9: Then it happened, as he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, that God changed his heart into another heart; and all these signs came to pass on that day.
verses.10:10: When they came there to Gibeah, look, a band of prophets was coming to meet him; and the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
verses.10:11: Now when all who knew him previously saw him, and there he was prophesying with prophets, the people said to one another, "What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:12: A man from there answered and said, "And who is their father?" Therefore it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:13: When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
verses.10:14: Now Saul's uncle said to him and to his attendant, "Where did you go?" And he said, "To search for the female donkeys; and when we saw that they were not there, we went to Samuel."
verses.10:15: Saul's uncle said, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."
verses.10:16: So Saul said to his uncle, "He plainly told us that the female donkeys had been found." Yet he did not tell him about the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel had spoken.
verses.10:17: Then Samuel summoned the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.10:18: And he said to the sons of Israel, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.'
verses.10:19: Yet today you have rejected your God, who Himself saves you from all your calamities and your distresses, and you have said to Him, 'Set a king over us!' Now therefore, present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands."
verses.10:20: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
verses.10:21: Then he brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken. And Saul the son of Kish was taken; yet they searched for him, and he was not found.
verses.10:22: So they inquired again of the LORD, "Has a man come here yet?" And the LORD said, "Look, he has hidden himself among the baggage."
verses.10:23: So they ran and took him from there; and when he took his stand in the midst of the people, he was taller than all the people from his shoulders and upward.
verses.10:24: Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? Surely there is no one like him among all the people." Then all the people shouted and said, "May the king live!"
verses.10:25: Then Samuel spoke to the people the ordinance of the kingdom, and wrote it in the scroll and placed it before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each man to his own house.
verses.10:26: Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and with him went the men of valor whose hearts God had touched.
verses.10:27: But worthless men said, "How can this one save us?" So they despised him and brought him no gift. Yet he was like one who keeps silent.
verses.11:1: Then Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."
verses.11:2: Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours, and I will place it as a reproach upon all Israel."
verses.11:3: The elders of Jabesh said to him, "Grant us seven days' respite, so that we may send messengers throughout all the territory of Israel; and if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you."
verses.11:4: Then the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the hearing of the people; and all the people lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.11:5: Now look, Saul was coming from the field behind the oxen, and Saul said, "What is the matter with the people, that they are weeping?" So they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
verses.11:6: Then the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned intensely.
verses.11:7: He took a yoke of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!" Then the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
verses.11:8: He mustered them at Bezek; and the sons of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.11:9: They said to the messengers who had come, "This is what you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will have deliverance.'" So the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.
verses.11:10: Then the men of Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us according to all that is good in your eyes."
verses.11:11: On the next day, Saul arranged the people into three divisions, and they came into the midst of the camp during the morning watch and struck down Ammon until the heat of the day. And those who were left scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
verses.11:12: Then the people said to Samuel, "Who is the one who said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Hand over the men, so that we may put them to death!"
verses.11:13: But Saul said, "Not a man shall be put to death on this day, for today the LORD has accomplished deliverance in Israel."
verses.11:14: Then Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there."
verses.11:15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they also sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
verses.12:1: And Samuel said to all Israel, "Look, I have listened to your voice regarding all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
verses.12:2: And now, see, the king is walking before you, while I have grown old and gray-headed, and here are my sons with you; and I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
verses.12:3: Here I am. Testify against me in the presence of the LORD and in the presence of His anointed one: whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I exploited, or whom have I crushed? And from whose hand have I taken a bribe to hide my eyes with it? Then I will restore it to you."
verses.12:4: And they said, "You have not exploited us, and you have not crushed us, nor have you taken anything from anyone's hand."
verses.12:5: Then he told them, "The LORD is a witness against you, and His anointed one is a witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand." And they said, "He is a witness."
verses.12:6: Samuel said to the people, "The LORD is the one who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought up your fathers from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:7: And now, take your stand, and let me enter into judgment with you before the LORD regarding all the righteous deeds of the LORD that He did for you and for your fathers.
verses.12:8: When Jacob came into Egypt, your fathers cried out to the LORD, and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron; and they brought your fathers out from Egypt and caused them to dwell in this place.
verses.12:9: Yet they forgot the LORD their God; so He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of Hazor's army, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they battled against them.
verses.12:10: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, for we have abandoned the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. And now, rescue us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve You.'
verses.12:11: So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and rescued you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you dwelt in safety.
verses.12:12: Yet when you saw that Nahash, the king of the sons of Ammon, was coming against you, you said to me, 'No! Instead, a king will reign over us,' even though the LORD your God was your king.
verses.12:13: And now, here is the king whom you chose, whom you asked for; and look, the LORD has placed a king over you.
verses.12:14: If you fear the LORD and serve Him, and listen to His voice and do not defy the command of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you will follow after the LORD your God.
verses.12:15: But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD, and you defy the command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your fathers.
verses.12:16: Now too, take your stand and see this great thing that the LORD is about to do before your eyes.
verses.12:17: Is today not the wheat harvest? I will call to the LORD, and He will send thunder and rain; so know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of the LORD in asking for a king for yourselves."
verses.12:18: Then Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain on that day; and all the people feared the LORD and Samuel very much.
verses.12:19: And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray on behalf of your servants to the LORD your God, so that we do not die, for to all our sins we have added evil in asking for a king for ourselves."
verses.12:20: Then Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid. You yourselves have done all this evil; only do not turn away from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with your whole heart.
verses.12:21: And do not turn away, for that would mean going after empty things, which cannot benefit and cannot rescue, because they are empty.
verses.12:22: For the LORD will not cast off His people for the sake of His great name, since the LORD has resolved to make you a people for Himself.
verses.12:23: As for me as well, far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray on your behalf; instead, I will teach you in the good and upright way.
verses.12:24: Only fear the LORD and serve Him in truth with your whole heart; for see what great things He has done with you.
verses.12:25: Yet if you indeed do evil, both you and your king will be swept away."
verses.13:2: And Saul chose for himself three thousand from Israel: two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin; as for the rest of the people, he sent them away, each man to his tents.
verses.13:3: Then Jonathan struck down the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard about it; and Saul sounded the ram's horn throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
verses.13:4: And all Israel heard it said, "Saul has struck down the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines." Then the people were summoned to follow Saul to Gilgal.
verses.13:5: Now the Philistines gathered together to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and troops in abundance like the sand on the shore of the sea. And they went up and encamped in Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
verses.13:6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, because the people were hard-pressed, the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in crags, in vaults, and in cisterns.
verses.13:7: And some Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead, while Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed after him in trembling.
verses.13:8: So he waited seven days for the appointed time fixed by Samuel, yet Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people scattered away from him.
verses.13:9: Then Saul said, "Bring the burnt offering and the peace offerings near to me." And he offered up the burnt offering.
verses.13:10: Now just as he finished offering up the burnt offering, there was Samuel coming; and Saul went out to meet him to greet him.
verses.13:11: And Samuel said, "What have you done?" Saul said, "Because I saw that the people had scattered away from me, and you did not come at the appointed time of the days, while the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
verses.13:12: and I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me to Gilgal, and I have not sought favor from the LORD.' So I constrained myself and offered up the burnt offering."
verses.13:13: Then Samuel said to Saul, "You have behaved foolishly. You did not keep the command of the LORD your God that He commanded you; for by now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
verses.13:14: And now your kingdom will not stand. The LORD has sought for Himself a man according to His own heart, and the LORD has commissioned him as ruler over His people, because you did not keep what the LORD commanded you."
verses.13:15: Then Samuel rose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
verses.13:16: And Saul, his son Jonathan, and the people who were found with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin, whereas the Philistines had encamped in Michmash.
verses.13:17: And the raiding force went out from the camp of the Philistines in three columns: one column turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual,
verses.13:18: and another column turned toward the road to Beth-horon, and another column turned toward the road to the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.13:19: Now no smith was to be found in the whole land of Israel, because the Philistines said, "Or else the Hebrews will make a sword or a spear."
verses.13:20: And all Israel went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, and his plow-blade.
verses.13:21: And the fee was a pim for the plowshares, for the mattocks, for a three-pronged fork, for the axes, and for setting the oxgoad.
verses.13:22: And it came about on the day of battle that no sword or spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, yet they were found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.
verses.13:23: Then the outpost of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.
verses.14:1: Now it came about one day that Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to the outpost of the Philistines that is on the far side." Yet he did not tell his father.
verses.14:2: Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah beneath the pomegranate tree that was in Migron, and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
verses.14:3: And Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, priest of the LORD in Shiloh, was bearing an ephod. Now the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.
verses.14:4: Now between the passes through which Jonathan sought to cross over to the outpost of the Philistines, there was a crag of rock on one side and a crag of rock on the other side; the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Seneh.
verses.14:5: The one crag was a steep pillar on the north, opposite Michmash, and the other was on the south, opposite Geba.
verses.14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for there is no hindrance for the LORD to save by many or by few."
verses.14:7: And his armor-bearer said to him, "Do all that is in your heart. Turn your way; here I am with you according to your heart."
verses.14:8: Then Jonathan said, "Look, we are crossing over to the men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
verses.14:9: If they say to us like this, 'Stay still until we reach you,' then we will stand in our place and will not go up to them.
verses.14:10: But if they say like this, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand; and this will be the sign for us."
verses.14:11: So both of them revealed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, and the Philistines said, "Look, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they hid themselves!"
verses.14:12: Then the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, "Come up to us, and we will let you know something." And Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Come up behind me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."
verses.14:13: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and his feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And they fell before Jonathan, while his armor-bearer was putting them to death behind him.
verses.14:14: And the first blow that Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck was about twenty men, within roughly half a furrow of a yoke of field.
verses.14:15: And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the outpost and the raiders trembled too. The earth quaked, and it became a trembling from God.
verses.14:16: And Saul's watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and look, the multitude was melting away and moving this way and that.
verses.14:17: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, "Count now and see who has gone from us." And they counted, and look, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
verses.14:18: Then Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ark of God near." For the ark of God was with the sons of Israel on that day.
verses.14:19: And it happened while Saul was speaking to the priest that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines kept growing greater and greater; so Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."
verses.14:20: Then Saul and all the people who were with him rallied together and came to the battle; and look, every man's sword was against his companion, a very great confusion.
verses.14:21: Now the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines previously, who had gone up with them into the camp all around, even they came to be with Israel who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.14:22: And all the men of Israel who were hiding themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they also pursued closely after them in the battle.
verses.14:23: So the LORD saved Israel on that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.
verses.14:24: Now the men of Israel were hard-pressed on that day, for Saul had bound the people under an oath, saying, "Cursed is the man who eats food until evening and until I have avenged myself on my enemies." So none of the people tasted food.
verses.14:25: And all the people of the land came into the forest, and there was honey on the surface of the field.
verses.14:26: When the people came to the forest, look, there was a flow of honey; yet no one brought his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
verses.14:27: But Jonathan had not heard when his father charged the people with the oath; so he stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb, and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
verses.14:28: Then a man from among the people spoke up and said, "Your father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats food today.'" And the people were faint.
verses.14:29: And Jonathan said, "My father has troubled the land. See now how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.14:30: How much more if the people had eaten freely today from the plunder of their enemies that they found! For then would not the blow against the Philistines have been greater?"
verses.14:31: And they struck down the Philistines on that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very faint.
verses.14:32: Then the people pounced upon the plunder, and they took sheep, cattle, and calves and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.
verses.14:33: Then they told Saul, saying, "Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood." And he said, "You have broken faith! Roll a large stone to me today."
verses.14:34: Then Saul said, "Spread out among the people and say to them, 'Bring to me, each man his ox and each man his sheep, and slaughter them here and eat, and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.'" verses.14:35: And Saul built an altar to the LORD; that one was the first altar he built to the LORD.
verses.14:36: Then Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder among them until the light of morning, and let us not leave a man among them." And they said, "Do all that is good in your eyes." But the priest said, "Let us draw near to God here."
verses.14:37: So Saul inquired of God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?" Yet He did not answer him on that day.
verses.14:38: Then Saul said, "Come near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see how this sin has happened today.
verses.14:39: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he will surely die!" Yet no one from all the people answered him.
verses.14:40: Then he said to all Israel, "You will be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side." And the people said to Saul, "Do what is good in your eyes."
verses.14:41: Then Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, "Give a true decision." And Jonathan and Saul were taken, while the people went free.
verses.14:42: And Saul said, "Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son." And Jonathan was taken.
verses.14:43: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." So Jonathan told him and said, "I did indeed taste a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am; I will die."
verses.14:44: And Saul said, "May God do so and add even more, for you will surely die, Jonathan!"
verses.14:45: But the people said to Saul, "Shall Jonathan die, who worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for he has worked with God on this day." So the people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.
verses.14:46: Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.14:47: Now Saul took the kingship over Israel, and he fought on every side against all his enemies: against Moab, against the sons of Ammon, against Edom, against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he dealt punishment.
verses.14:48: And he acted valiantly, struck down Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered them.
verses.14:49: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger was Michal.
verses.14:50: And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz, and the name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
verses.14:51: Now Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, was the son of Abiel.
verses.14:52: Now the war against the Philistines was fierce all the days of Saul; and whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any man of valor, he gathered him to himself.
verses.15:1: Samuel said to Saul, "It was me the LORD sent to anoint you as king over His people, over Israel. Now then, listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.
verses.15:2: This is what the LORD of hosts says: 'I have called to account what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when Israel came up from Egypt.
verses.15:3: Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to complete destruction all that belongs to him; do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, young child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"
verses.15:4: So Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.15:5: Saul came as far as the city of Amalek and set an ambush in the valley.
verses.15:6: Then Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, so that I do not sweep you away with them; for you showed loyal kindness to all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt." So the Kenites departed from among Amalek.
verses.15:7: Then Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as one goes toward Shur, which lies east of Egypt.
verses.15:8: He seized Agag the king of Amalek alive, and all the people he devoted to complete destruction by the edge of the sword.
verses.15:9: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle, the second-born and the lambs, and all that was good, and they were not willing to devote them to complete destruction; yet all the property that was despised and worthless, that they devoted to complete destruction.
verses.15:10: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
verses.15:11: "I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me and has not carried out My words." And Samuel became angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
verses.15:12: Samuel rose early in the morning to meet Saul, and it was reported to Samuel, saying, "Saul went to Carmel, and look, he has set up a monument for himself; then he turned around, passed on, and went down to Gilgal."
verses.15:13: Then Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you by the LORD! I have carried out the word of the LORD."
verses.15:14: But Samuel said, "Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of cattle that I am hearing?"
verses.15:15: Saul said, "They have brought them from the Amalekites, because the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice to the LORD your God; and the rest we have devoted to complete destruction."
verses.15:16: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Stop, and let me tell you what the LORD spoke to me last night." And he said to him, "Speak."
verses.15:17: Samuel said, "Though you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as king over Israel.
verses.15:18: And the LORD sent you on a journey and said, 'Go and devote the sinners, Amalek, to complete destruction, and fight against them until they are completely consumed.'
verses.15:19: Why then did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but swooped down upon the plunder and did what is evil in the eyes of the LORD?"
verses.15:20: Saul said to Samuel, "Indeed, I did listen to the voice of the LORD, and I went on the journey on which the LORD sent me; I brought Agag the king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to complete destruction.
verses.15:21: Yet the people took from the plunder sheep and cattle, the choicest of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal."
verses.15:22: Then Samuel said, "Does the LORD take as much pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? Look, listening is better than sacrifice, and paying attention than the fat of rams.
verses.15:23: For rebellion is the sin of divination, and stubbornness is wickedness and household idols. Since you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you from being king."
verses.15:24: Then Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have violated the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.15:25: Now then, please pardon my sin, and return with me so that I may bow in worship to the LORD."
verses.15:26: Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."
verses.15:27: As Samuel turned around to go, Saul grasped the corner of his robe, and it tore.
verses.15:28: Then Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingship of Israel away from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
verses.15:29: Moreover, the Splendor of Israel will not deal falsely and will not feel regret, for He is not a human being to feel regret."
verses.15:30: He said, "I have sinned; now please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, and I will bow in worship to the LORD your God."
verses.15:31: So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul bowed in worship to the LORD.
verses.15:32: Then Samuel said, "Bring Agag the king of Amalek here to me." And Agag walked to him confidently, and Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death has departed."
verses.15:33: Samuel said, "Just as your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women." Then Samuel hacked Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
verses.15:34: Then Samuel went to Ramah, while Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
verses.15:35: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. And the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.16:1: Then the LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn over Saul, seeing that I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen a king for Myself among his sons."
verses.16:2: Samuel said, "How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me." And the LORD said, "Take a heifer from the herd with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'
verses.16:3: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I Myself will make known to you what you are to do; and anoint for Me the one whom I tell you."
verses.16:4: So Samuel did what the LORD had spoken and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, "Is your coming in peace?"
verses.16:5: He said, "In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
verses.16:6: When they arrived, he saw Eliab and said, "Surely His anointed is before the LORD."
verses.16:7: But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not gaze at his appearance or at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For it is not what a human sees; indeed, a human sees what meets the eyes, whereas the LORD sees into the heart."
verses.16:8: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel. And he said, "This one too the LORD has not chosen."
verses.16:9: Next Jesse had Shammah pass by. And he said, "This one too the LORD has not chosen."
verses.16:10: So Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."
verses.16:11: Samuel said to Jesse, "Are these all the young men?" And he said, "There still remains the youngest, and look, he is tending the sheep." Then Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and fetch him, for we will not sit down until he arrives here."
verses.16:12: So he sent and brought him in. He was ruddy, with handsome eyes and a pleasing appearance. And the LORD said, "Rise up, anoint him, for this is the one."
verses.16:13: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day onward. Then Samuel rose and went to Ramah.
verses.16:14: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him.
verses.16:15: Saul's servants said to him, "Look now, an evil spirit from God is terrifying you.
verses.16:16: Let our lord please give the command, and your servants before you will seek out a man who knows how to play the lyre. Then whenever an evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play with his hand, and it will be well with you."
verses.16:17: So Saul said to his servants, "Please look for a man for me who plays well, and bring him to me."
verses.16:18: One of the young men answered and said, "Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, discerning in speech, and a man of fine appearance; and the LORD is with him."
verses.16:19: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who is with the sheep."
verses.16:20: Then Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by the hand of his son David to Saul.
verses.16:21: So David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.
verses.16:22: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, "Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes."
verses.16:23: So whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would take the lyre and play with his hand; then Saul would be refreshed and it would be well with him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
verses.17:1: The Philistines gathered their forces for battle, and they assembled at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.
verses.17:2: Saul and the men of Israel assembled and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and they drew up for battle to meet the Philistines.
verses.17:3: The Philistines were standing on the mountain on this side, and Israel was standing on the mountain on that side, and the ravine was between them.
verses.17:4: A champion stepped out from the camps of the Philistines; his name was Goliath, from Gath, and his height was six cubits and a span.
verses.17:5: A bronze helmet was on his head, and he was dressed in a coat of scale armor; the weight of the coat of armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.
verses.17:6: Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze javelin was between his shoulders.
verses.17:7: The wooden shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam, and the blade of his spear was six hundred shekels of iron; and the one carrying the large shield walked ahead of him.
verses.17:8: He stood and called out to the battle lines of Israel and said to them, "Why are you coming out to draw up for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and you are servants of Saul? Select a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
verses.17:9: If he is able to fight with me and strikes me down, then we will be servants to you; but if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you will be servants to us and will serve us."
verses.17:10: Then the Philistine said, "I taunt the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together."
verses.17:11: And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and very afraid.
verses.17:32: Then David said to Saul, "Let no one's heart sink on his account. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."
verses.17:33: Saul said to David, "You cannot go against this Philistine to fight with him, because you are a youth, while he has been a man of war from his youth."
verses.17:34: David said to Saul, "Your servant has been tending the sheep for his father, and whenever a lion or a bear would come and carry off a lamb from the flock,
verses.17:35: I would go out after it, strike it, and rescue it from its mouth; and when it rose up against me, I would seize it by its beard, strike it, and put it to death.
verses.17:36: Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has taunted the battle lines of the living God."
verses.17:37: And David said, "The LORD, who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Then Saul said to David, "Go, and may the LORD be with you."
verses.17:38: Saul dressed David in his garments, placed a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in a coat of armor.
verses.17:39: David fastened his sword over his garments and tried to walk, because he had not tested them. Then David said to Saul, "I cannot walk in these, because I have not tested them." So David removed them from himself.
verses.17:40: Then he took his staff in his hand, selected for himself five smooth stones from the streambed, and placed them in his shepherd's bag, in the pouch; with his sling in his hand, he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.17:42: The Philistine looked intently and saw David, and he despised him, because he was a youth, ruddy and of handsome appearance.
verses.17:43: Then the Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you are coming at me with staffs?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.17:44: And the Philistine said to David, "Come here to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field."
verses.17:45: David said to the Philistine, "You are coming to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin, but I am coming to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have taunted.
verses.17:46: This day the LORD will surrender you into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from you; and this day I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines to the birds of the heavens and to the wild beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that Israel has a God,
verses.17:47: and this entire assembly will know that the LORD does not save by sword or by spear; for the battle belongs to the LORD, and He will give you into our hand."
verses.17:48: When the Philistine rose up, came forward, and approached to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.
verses.17:49: David reached his hand into the bag, took a stone from there, slung it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead; the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell face down to the ground.
verses.17:51: David ran and stood over the Philistine; he took his sword, pulled it from its sheath, put him to death, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their mighty warrior was dead, they fled.
verses.17:52: Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up, raised a battle shout, and pursued the Philistines as far as the approach to a valley and as far as the gates of Ekron; and the fatally wounded of the Philistines fell along the road to Shaaraim, as far as Gath and as far as Ekron.
verses.17:53: The sons of Israel turned back from hotly pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camps.
verses.17:54: And David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, while he placed his weapons in his tent.
verses.18:6: Now as they were arriving, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing to meet King Saul, with tambourines, with gladness, and with three-stringed instruments.
verses.18:7: The celebrating women sang back and forth and said, "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands."
verses.18:8: Saul grew very angry, and this saying was displeasing in his eyes; he said, "They have given David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands. Now what remains for him is only the kingdom."
verses.18:9: So Saul kept eyeing David from that day onward.
verses.18:12: Now Saul feared David, because the LORD was with him, while He had withdrawn from Saul.
verses.18:13: So Saul removed him from being with him and appointed him as commander of a thousand for himself; and he went out and came in before the people.
verses.18:14: David was succeeding in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.
verses.18:15: When Saul saw that he was succeeding greatly, he stood in dread of him.
verses.18:16: All Israel and Judah, however, loved David, because he was the one going out and coming in before them.
verses.18:20: Now Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved David; and they told Saul, and the matter was right in his eyes.
verses.18:21: Saul said, "I will give her to him, that she may become a snare for him and the hand of the Philistines may be against him." Then Saul said to David, "A second time you will become my son-in-law today."
verses.18:22: Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David in secret, saying, 'See, the king takes pleasure in you, and all his servants love you; so now, become the king's son-in-law.'"
verses.18:23: Saul's servants spoke these words in David's ears, and David said, "Is it a light matter in your eyes to become the king's son-in-law, when I am a poor man and lightly regarded?"
verses.18:24: Then Saul's servants reported to him, saying, "David spoke words like these."
verses.18:25: Saul said, "This is what you are to say to David, 'The king has no desire for a bride-price, but rather for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to avenge himself on the king's enemies.'" Now Saul schemed to cause David to fall by the hand of the Philistines.
verses.18:26: His servants told David these words, and the matter was right in David's eyes to become the king's son-in-law; and the days had not yet expired.
verses.18:27: So David rose up and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred men among the Philistines. David brought their foreskins, and they counted them out in full to the king so that he might become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal as a wife.
verses.18:28: Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved him.
verses.18:29: So Saul feared David even more, and Saul remained an enemy to David always.
verses.19:1: Saul spoke to his son Jonathan and to all his servants about putting David to death, yet Jonathan the son of Saul delighted greatly in David.
verses.19:2: So Jonathan told David, saying, "My father Saul is seeking to put you to death. Now then, please be on your guard in the morning; stay in a secret place and hide yourself.
verses.19:3: I will go out and stand at my father's side in the field where you are, and I myself will speak about you to my father; whatever I see, I will tell you."
verses.19:4: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, "Let the king not sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds have been very good for you.
verses.19:5: He placed his life in his hand and struck the Philistine, and the LORD accomplished a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced; why then should you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death for no reason?"
verses.19:6: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, "As the LORD lives, he will not be put to death."
verses.19:7: Then Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as previously.
verses.19:8: Once more war broke out, and David went out and fought against the Philistines; he dealt them a great blow, and they fled from before him.
verses.19:9: Then an evil spirit from the LORD came upon Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, while David was playing music with his hand.
verses.19:10: Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slipped away from before Saul, and Saul struck the spear into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.
