verses.19:11: Then Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and to put him to death in the morning. But his wife Michal told David, saying, "If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death."
verses.19:12: So Michal lowered David through the window, and he went away, fled, and escaped.
verses.19:13: Michal took the household idol and placed it in the bed; she put a cushion of goats' hair at its head and covered it with the cloth.
verses.19:14: Then Saul sent messengers to take David, but she said, "He is ill."
verses.19:15: So Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me in the bed to put him to death."
verses.19:16: The messengers came in, and there was the household idol in the bed, with the cushion of goats' hair at its head.
verses.19:17: Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this and sent my enemy away, so that he escaped?" Michal said to Saul, "He himself said to me, 'Let me go! Why should I put you to death?'"
verses.19:18: Now David had fled and escaped; he came to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.
verses.19:19: It was reported to Saul, "Look, David is at Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David; and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing and presiding over them, the Spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:21: When they told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. Once again Saul sent a third group of messengers, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:22: Then he himself also went to Ramah and came as far as the great cistern that is in Secu. He inquired and said, "Where are Samuel and David?" And someone said, "Look, they are at Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:23: So he went there, to Naioth in Ramah. And the Spirit of God came upon him too, and he walked along continuously, prophesying until he arrived at Naioth in Ramah.
verses.19:24: He also stripped off his garments, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and fell down naked all that day and all night. Therefore people say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.20:1: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and he came and said before Jonathan, "What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he is seeking my life?"
verses.20:2: He said to him, "Far be it! You will not die. Look, my father does not do anything great or small without disclosing it to me. Why then would my father hide this matter from me? It is not so."
verses.20:3: Yet David swore further and said, "Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, 'Let Jonathan not know this, or he will be grieved.' Yet truly, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is merely a step between me and death."
verses.20:4: Then Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul says, I will do for you."
verses.20:5: So David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow is the new moon, and I ought surely to sit with the king to eat; yet let me go, and I will hide in the field until the third evening.
verses.20:6: If your father misses me at all, then say, 'David earnestly asked my permission to run to Bethlehem, his city, because the yearly sacrifice for the whole family is there.'
verses.20:7: If he says this, 'Good,' then there is peace for your servant; but if he grows exceedingly angry, know that harm has been determined by him.
verses.20:8: Therefore show faithful love to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with yourself. Yet if there is iniquity in me, put me to death yourself; why should you bring me to your father?"
verses.20:9: Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! For if I knew for certain that harm had been determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you of it?"
verses.20:10: Then David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me, or what if your father answers you harshly?"
verses.20:11: Jonathan said to David, "Come, let us go out into the field." So the two of them went out into the field.
verses.20:12: Then Jonathan said to David, "By the LORD, the God of Israel, when I sound out my father about this time tomorrow or the third day, look, if things are good toward David and I do not then send to you and disclose it to you,
verses.20:13: may the LORD do so to Jonathan, and may He add still more! And if it pleases my father to bring harm upon you, I will disclose it to you and send you away, so that you may go in peace. May the LORD be with you, just as He was with my father.
verses.20:14: And if I am still alive, will you not show the faithful love of the LORD toward me, so that I do not die?
verses.20:15: And do not cut off your faithful love from my house forever, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth."
verses.20:16: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David: "May the LORD require it from the hand of David's enemies."
verses.20:17: Once again Jonathan had David swear by his love for him, because he loved him with the love of his own soul.
verses.20:18: Then Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be found empty.
verses.20:19: On the third day, go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself on the day of the deed, and remain beside the stone Ezel.
verses.20:20: And I myself will shoot three arrows to its side, as though I were shooting at a target.
verses.20:21: Now I will send the boy: 'Go, find the arrows.' If I expressly say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are on this side of you; take them,' then come, for there is peace for you and nothing is wrong, as the LORD lives.
verses.20:22: But if I say this to the youth, 'Look, the arrows are beyond you,' then go, for the LORD has sent you away.
verses.20:23: And as for the matter of which you and I have spoken, see, the LORD is between me and you forever."
verses.20:24: So David hid in the field. When the new moon came, the king sat down to the meal to eat.
verses.20:25: The king sat on his seat as at other times, on the seat by the wall; Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat at Saul's side, but David's place was empty.
verses.20:26: Yet Saul did not speak anything on that day, for he thought, "Something has happened; he is not clean; surely he is not clean."
verses.20:27: On the day after the new moon, the second day, David's place was empty. So Saul said to his son Jonathan, "Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"
verses.20:28: Jonathan answered Saul, "David earnestly asked my permission to go to Bethlehem.
verses.20:29: He said, 'Please let me go, because we have a family sacrifice in the city, and my brother himself has commanded me to come. Now then, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me slip away and see my brothers.' That is why he has not come to the king's table."
verses.20:30: Then Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, "You son of a wayward, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you are choosing the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
verses.20:31: For all the days that the son of Jesse lives upon the earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. So now, send and bring him to me, for he is doomed to die!"
verses.20:32: Jonathan answered his father Saul and said to him, "Why is he to be put to death? What has he done?"
verses.20:33: Then Saul hurled the spear at him to strike him down, and Jonathan knew that it had been determined by his father to put David to death.
verses.20:34: Jonathan rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food on the second day of the new moon, because he was grieved over David, since his father had disgraced him.
verses.20:35: In the morning, Jonathan went out into the field for his appointment with David, and a young boy was with him.
verses.20:36: He said to his boy, "Run, please find the arrows that I am about to shoot." As the boy ran, he shot the arrow to pass beyond him.
verses.20:37: When the boy arrived at the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called out after the boy and said, "Is the arrow not beyond you?"
verses.20:38: And Jonathan called out after the boy, "Quickly! Hurry! Do not stop!" So Jonathan's boy gathered the arrows and came to his master.
verses.20:39: Yet the boy did not know anything; Jonathan and David alone knew the matter.
verses.20:40: Then Jonathan handed his weapons to his boy and said to him, "Go, carry them into the city."
verses.20:41: As soon as the boy had left, David rose from the south side, fell on his face to the ground, and bowed down three times. They kissed one another and wept with one another, and David wept all the more.
verses.20:42: Then Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace, since both of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD will be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring forever.'"
verses.21:1: Then he rose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.
verses.21:2: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest, and Ahimelech trembled on going to meet David and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no man is with you?"
verses.21:3: And David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king charged me with a matter and said to me, 'Let no man know anything about the matter on which I am sending you and which I have commanded you.' And I have directed the young men to such and such a place.
verses.21:4: Now then, what is under your hand? Give five loaves of bread into my hand, or whatever is found."
verses.21:5: The priest answered David and said, "There is no ordinary bread under my hand, but there is holy bread, if the young men have kept themselves at least from women."
verses.21:6: David answered the priest and said to him, "Truly women have been kept back from us as before when I set out, and the vessels of the young men are holy, even though it is an ordinary journey; how much more today will it be holy in the vessel!"
verses.21:7: So the priest gave him what was holy, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD to set out hot bread on the day it was taken away.
verses.21:8: Now a man from Saul's servants was there on that day, detained before the LORD; his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.
verses.21:9: And David said to Ahimelech, "Is there not here under your hand a spear or a sword? For I took neither my sword nor my weapons in my hand, because the king's matter was urgent."
verses.21:10: Then the priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah, here it is, wrapped in a garment behind the ephod. If you would take that for yourself, take it, for there is no other except it here." And David said, "There is none like it; give it to me."
verses.21:11: Then David rose and fled that day from before Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath.
verses.21:12: And the servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, king of the land? Did they not sing to one another about this man in the dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.21:13: David laid these words in his heart, and he was greatly afraid of Achish king of Gath.
verses.21:14: So he changed his demeanor before their eyes and acted like a madman in their hands; he scratched marks on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down onto his beard.
verses.21:15: Then Achish said to his servants, "Look, you see a man acting madly; why are you bringing him to me?
verses.21:16: Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this fellow to act madly in my presence? Shall this one come into my house?"
verses.22:1: So David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father's house heard, they went down to him there.
verses.22:2: Every man in distress, every man who had a creditor, and every man bitter of soul gathered to him, and he became commander over them. There were about four hundred men with him.
verses.22:3: David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother come out and be with you, until I know what God will do for me."
verses.22:4: So he brought them before the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
verses.22:5: Then Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold; go and enter the land of Judah." So David departed and came into the forest of Hereth.
verses.22:6: Then Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
verses.22:7: Saul said to his servants who were standing around him, "Listen now, Benjaminites! Will the son of Jesse give fields and vineyards to all of you as well? Will he appoint all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds,
verses.22:8: that all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reveals to my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse, and there is no one among you who grieves for me and reveals to my ear that my son has raised up my servant against me to lie in ambush, as at this day?"
verses.22:9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing beside Saul's servants, answered and said, "I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
verses.22:10: He inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
verses.22:11: Then the king sent to summon Ahimelech son of Ahitub the priest, along with all his father's house, the priests who were in Nob, and all of them came to the king.
verses.22:12: Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." And he said, "Here I am, my lord."
verses.22:13: Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, that he should rise against me to lie in ambush, as at this day?"
verses.22:14: Then Ahimelech answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king's son-in-law, who turns to your bidding and is honored in your house?
verses.22:15: Did I begin today to inquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king lay anything against his servant or against all my father's house, for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great."
verses.22:16: Then the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house."
verses.22:17: And the king said to the guards who were standing around him, "Turn and put to death the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not reveal it to my ear." But the king's servants were not willing to stretch out their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.
verses.22:18: Then the king said to Doeg, "You turn and fall upon the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon the priests himself, and he put to death on that day eighty-five men who wore a linen ephod.
verses.22:19: And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword, both man and woman, child and nursing infant, and ox, donkey, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
verses.22:20: But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was Abiathar, and he fled after David.
verses.22:21: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
verses.22:22: Then David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I myself have brought this upon every life of your father's house.
verses.22:23: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for the one who seeks my life seeks your life, for with me you are in safekeeping."
verses.23:1: Then they told David, saying, "Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors."
verses.23:2: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And the LORD said to David, "Go and strike the Philistines, and deliver Keilah."
verses.23:3: But David's men said to him, "Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the battle lines of the Philistines!"
verses.23:4: So David inquired of the LORD yet again, and the LORD answered him and said, "Rise, go down to Keilah, for I am giving the Philistines into your hand."
verses.23:5: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines; he drove off their livestock and struck them with a great blow. Thus David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.23:6: Now it happened, when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that an ephod came down in his hand.
verses.23:7: When it was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah, Saul said, "God has handed him over into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a city with doors and a bar."
verses.23:8: So Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
verses.23:9: Now David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, so he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod near."
verses.23:10: Then David said, "LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has surely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account.
verses.23:11: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, just as Your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant." And the LORD said, "He will come down."
verses.23:13: Then David and his men, about six hundred men, rose and went out from Keilah, and they moved about wherever they could go. When it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, he refrained from going out.
verses.23:14: David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and stayed in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God did not give him into his hand.
verses.23:15: Now David saw that Saul had gone out to seek his life, while David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.
verses.23:16: Then Jonathan son of Saul rose and went to David at Horesh, and he strengthened his hand in God.
verses.23:17: He said to him, "Do not be afraid, for the hand of my father Saul will not find you; you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you, and my father Saul knows this as well."
verses.23:18: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD; David stayed at Horesh, while Jonathan went to his house.
verses.23:19: Then Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is David not hiding himself among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is south of Jeshimon?
verses.23:20: And now, king, according to all the desire of your soul to come down, come down; and it will be our part to surrender him into the hand of the king."
verses.23:21: And Saul said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
verses.23:22: Go now, make even more certain, and know and see his place where his foot is, and who has seen him there; for it has been told to me that he is very crafty.
verses.23:23: Therefore see and learn of all the hiding places where he hides himself, and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you. And if he is in the land, then I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."
verses.23:24: So they rose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.
verses.23:25: Then Saul and his men went to search, and they told David; so he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard of it, he pursued after David into the wilderness of Maon.
verses.23:26: Saul went along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to capture them.
verses.23:27: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land!"
verses.23:28: So Saul turned back from pursuing after David and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place the Rock of Divisions.
verses.24:1: Then David went up from there and stayed among the strongholds of En Gedi.
verses.24:2: Now when Saul returned from following after the Philistines, they reported to him, saying, "Look, David is in the wilderness of En Gedi."
verses.24:3: So Saul took three thousand picked men out of all Israel and went to seek David and his men before the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
verses.24:4: He came to the sheepfolds alongside the road, where there was a cave, and Saul went inside to relieve himself, while David and his men were sitting in the far recesses of the cave.
verses.24:5: Then David's men said to him, "Here is the day about which the LORD said to you, 'Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as seems good in your eyes.'" So David rose and stealthily cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
verses.24:6: Afterward, David's heart struck him because he had cut off the corner belonging to Saul.
verses.24:7: He said to his men, "Far be it from me, before the LORD, that I should do this thing to my lord, to the anointed of the LORD, to extend my hand against him, for he is the anointed of the LORD."
verses.24:8: So David checked his men with these words and did not allow them to rise against Saul. Then Saul rose from the cave and went along the road.
verses.24:9: Afterward David rose, went out of the cave, and called after Saul, saying, "My lord the king!" When Saul looked behind him, David bent low with his face to the ground and bowed down.
verses.24:10: David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of people saying, 'Look, David is seeking your harm'?
verses.24:11: Look, this day your eyes have seen how the LORD gave you into my hand today in the cave. Someone said to kill you, yet my eye spared you, and I said, 'I will not extend my hand against my lord, for he is the anointed of the LORD.'
verses.24:12: And my father, look! Yes, look at the corner of your robe in my hand! Because I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you, know and see that there is no evil or transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, yet you are hunting for my life to take it.
verses.24:13: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me from you, yet my hand will not be against you.
verses.24:14: Just as the ancient proverb says, 'From wicked people comes wickedness,' yet my hand will not be against you.
verses.24:15: After whom has the king of Israel gone out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog? After a single flea?
verses.24:16: So may the LORD be arbiter and judge between me and you; may He see and plead my cause, and vindicate me from your hand."
verses.24:17: Now it happened, as David finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" Then Saul raised his voice and wept.
verses.24:18: And he said to David, "You are more righteous than I am, for you have rendered good to me, while I have rendered evil to you.
verses.24:19: And you have made known today the good that you have done with me, in that the LORD turned me over into your hand, yet you did not kill me.
verses.24:20: For when a man finds his enemy, does he send him off on a good way? So may the LORD repay you with good in return for what you have done for me this day.
verses.24:21: And now, look, I know that you will surely reign, and the kingdom of Israel will stand firm in your hand.
verses.24:22: And now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me and that you will not wipe out my name from the house of my father."
verses.24:23: So David swore to Saul, and Saul went to his house, while David and his men went up to the stronghold.
verses.25:1: Now Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and lamented for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. Then David rose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.25:2: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. The man was very great; he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
verses.25:3: Now the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. The woman was of good insight and lovely in form, whereas the man was harsh and evil in his deeds, and he was a Calebite.
verses.25:4: Then David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
verses.25:5: So David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal, and ask after his welfare in my name.
verses.25:6: And thus you shall say: 'To life! Peace be to you, peace to your house, and peace to everything that belongs to you.
verses.25:7: And now I have heard that you have shearers. Now, your shepherds have been with us; we did not mistreat them, nor did anything of theirs go missing all the days they were in Carmel.
verses.25:8: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. May the young men then find favor in your eyes, since we have come on a festive day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David.'"
verses.25:9: Then David's young men came, spoke to Nabal in accordance with all these words in the name of David, and waited.
verses.25:10: But Nabal answered the servants of David and said, "Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse? Today servants are numerous who are breaking away, each man from his master.
verses.25:11: Should I then take my bread and my water and my butchered meat that I have butchered for my shearers, and give them to men when I do not know where they are from?"
verses.25:12: So David's young men turned back along their way; they returned and came and told him in accordance with all these words.
verses.25:13: Then David said to his men, "Each man, strap on his sword!" So each man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. And about four hundred men went up after David, while two hundred stayed by the baggage.
verses.25:14: Meanwhile, one of the young men reported to Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, "Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, yet he lashed out at them.
verses.25:15: Yet the men were very good to us; we were not mistreated, nor did we miss anything all the days we moved about with them while we were in the field.
verses.25:16: They were a wall around us both by night and by day, all the days we were with them shepherding the sheep.
verses.25:17: And now, know and see what you should do, for harm is fully determined against our master and against all his house, and he is too worthless a man for anyone to speak to him."
verses.25:18: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five prepared sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and set them on the donkeys.
verses.25:19: She said to her young men, "Go on ahead of me; look, I am coming behind you." However, she did not tell her husband Nabal.
verses.25:20: And as she was riding on the donkey and going down under cover of the mountain, look, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
verses.25:21: Now David had said, "Surely for nothing I guarded everything belonging to this fellow in the wilderness, so that nothing of all that is his went missing, yet he has returned evil to me in exchange for good.
verses.25:22: May God do so to the enemies of David, and may He do even more, if I leave remaining by morning of all that belongs to him one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:23: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and came down off the donkey, fell upon her face before David, and bowed down to the ground.
verses.25:24: She fell at his feet and said, "Upon me, upon me myself, my lord, be the guilt! Please let your maidservant speak in your hearing, and listen to the words of your maidservant.
verses.25:25: Please do not let my lord give his mind to this worthless man, to Nabal, for just as his name is, so is he: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. Yet I, your maidservant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.
verses.25:26: And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has kept you back from incurring bloodguilt and from saving yourself by your own hand, now may your enemies and those who seek harm against my lord become like Nabal.
verses.25:27: And now, as for this blessing that your servant woman has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men who walk in the footsteps of my lord.
verses.25:28: Please pardon the transgression of your maidservant; for the LORD will surely make a lasting house for my lord, since my lord fights the LORD's battles, and no evil will be found in you throughout your days.
verses.25:29: And if someone rises to pursue you and to seek your life, the life of my lord will be bound up in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, whereas the life of your enemies He will sling out from within the pocket of the sling.
verses.25:30: And it will happen, when the LORD has done for my lord in accordance with all the good that He has spoken about you and has appointed you as leader over Israel,
verses.25:31: that this will not become for you a cause of faltering or a stumbling block of heart for my lord, by having shed blood without cause or by my lord having saved himself. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, then remember your maidservant."
verses.25:32: So David said to Abigail, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!
verses.25:33: And blessed is your good sense, and blessed are you, who have restrained me this day from incurring bloodguilt and from saving myself by my own hand.
verses.25:34: For indeed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has kept me back from harming you, had you not hurried and come to meet me, surely by the light of morning there would not have been left to Nabal one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:35: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have granted you favor."
verses.25:36: Then Abigail came to Nabal, and look, he had a banquet in his house like the banquet of a king. Nabal's heart was cheerful within him, and he was exceedingly drunk; so she told him nothing, small or great, until the light of morning.
verses.25:37: And it happened in the morning, once the wine had gone out from Nabal, that his wife told him these matters; then his heart died inside him, and he became like a stone.
verses.25:38: Then it happened about ten days later that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.25:39: When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, "Blessed is the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from Nabal's hand and has held back His servant from evil; and the LORD has returned Nabal's evil upon his own head." Then David sent and spoke for Abigail, to take her to himself as a wife.
verses.25:40: So David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you to take you to himself as a wife."
verses.25:41: She rose, bowed down with her face to the ground, and said, "Here is your maidservant as a slave woman, to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."
verses.25:42: Then Abigail hurried and got up, and she rode on the donkey with her five young women who followed behind her; she went after the messengers of David and became his wife.
verses.25:43: David also took Ahinoam from Jezreel, and the two of them both became his wives.
verses.25:44: Meanwhile, Saul had given his daughter Michal, the wife of David, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
verses.26:1: Now the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is David not hiding himself on the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon?"
verses.26:2: Then Saul rose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and three thousand picked men of Israel were with him, to search for David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.26:3: Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which faces Jeshimon, along the road. Meanwhile David was staying in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
verses.26:4: David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had come for certain.
verses.26:5: Then David rose and came to the place where Saul had camped. David saw the place where Saul lay, with Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army; Saul was lying within the encampment, and the people were camping all around him.
verses.26:6: Then David spoke up and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, "Who will go down with me to Saul, to the camp?" Abishai replied, "I will go down with you."
verses.26:7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and look, Saul was lying asleep within the encampment, with his spear thrust into the ground at his head, and Abner and the people were lying all around him.
verses.26:8: Then Abishai said to David, "God has handed your enemy over into your hand today. Now then, please let me strike him to the ground with the spear in one stroke, and I will not do it to him a second time."
verses.26:9: David told Abishai, "Do not destroy him! For who has reached out his hand against the LORD's anointed and gone unpunished?"
verses.26:10: And David said, "As the LORD lives, the LORD will surely strike him down, or his day will arrive and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.
verses.26:11: Far be it from me before the LORD to reach out my hand against the LORD's anointed! Now then, please take the spear that is at his head and the flask of water, and let us go our way."
verses.26:12: So David took the spear and the flask of water from by Saul's head, and they went their way. No one saw, no one knew, and no one woke up, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.
verses.26:13: Then David crossed to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain at a distance, with a wide space between them.
verses.26:14: David called out to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" Abner responded and said, "Who are you, calling out to the king?"
verses.26:15: David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept guard over your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king, your lord.
verses.26:16: This thing you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you certainly deserve to die, because you have not kept guard over your lord, over the LORD's anointed. Now look where the king's spear is, and the flask of water that was at his head!"
verses.26:17: Saul recognized the voice of David and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David replied, "It is my voice, my lord the king."
verses.26:18: He went on to say, "Why then is my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done, and what evil is in my hand?
verses.26:19: Now then, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, may He smell an offering; but if the sons of men have, cursed are they before the LORD, because today they have driven me out from attaching myself to the inheritance of the LORD, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
verses.26:20: Now therefore, do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to search for a single flea, just as one pursues a partridge in the mountains."
verses.26:21: Saul replied, "I have sinned. Come back, my son David, for I will not harm you anymore, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have gone very far astray."
verses.26:22: David answered and said, "Here is the king's spear! Let one of the young men cross over and take it.
verses.26:23: The LORD will repay each man for his righteousness and his faithfulness; for the LORD gave you into my hand today, yet I was unwilling to reach out my hand against the LORD's anointed.
verses.26:24: Now look, just as your life was greatly valued in my eyes this day, so may my life be greatly valued in the eyes of the LORD, and may He rescue me from every distress."
verses.26:25: Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David! You will both surely act and surely prevail." So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.27:1: Then David said in his heart, "Now I will be swept away one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I surely escape to the land of the Philistines; then Saul will despair of searching for me anymore within all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand."
verses.27:2: Then David rose and crossed over - he and the six hundred men who were with him - to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
verses.27:3: And David lived with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's wife.
verses.27:4: Now it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, so he did not continue to search for him anymore.
verses.27:5: Then David said to Achish, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the towns of the countryside so that I may live there; for why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"
verses.27:6: So on that day Achish gave Ziklag to him; for this reason Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah until this day.
verses.27:7: Now the number of days that David lived in the countryside of the Philistines was a year and four months.
verses.27:8: Now David and his men went up and made raids against the Geshurites, the Gizrites, and the Amalekites; for they were the inhabitants of the land from ancient times, as you go toward Shur and as far as the land of Egypt.
verses.27:9: And David would strike the land and would leave neither man nor woman alive, and he would take sheep and cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing; then he would return and come to Achish.
verses.27:10: And Achish would say, "Did you not make a raid today?" And David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah, against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and against the Negev of the Kenites."
verses.27:11: David would leave neither man nor woman alive to bring to Gath, thinking, "Otherwise they might report against us, saying, 'This is what David did.'" And such was his practice all the days that he lived in the countryside of the Philistines.
verses.27:12: So Achish trusted David, thinking, "He has utterly made himself a stench among his people, in Israel, and he will be my servant forever."
verses.28:1: Now it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered their armies for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, "Know for certain that you will go out with me in the army, you and your men."
verses.28:2: David said to Achish, "Then you yourself will know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Then I will appoint you guard for my head for all time."
verses.28:3: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had lamented for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
verses.28:4: The Philistines assembled, came, and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa.
verses.28:5: Saul saw the Philistine camp; he was frightened, and his heart shuddered greatly.
verses.28:6: So Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, whether by dreams, by Urim, or by the prophets.
verses.28:7: Then Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire through her." And his servants said to him, "Look, there is a woman who is a medium at Endor."
verses.28:8: So Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. He said, "Please divine for me by a spirit of the dead, and bring up for me the one I tell you."
verses.28:9: But the woman said to him, "Look, you yourself know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you laying a snare for my life, to put me to death?"
verses.28:10: Then Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, "As the LORD lives, no punishment will come upon you for this matter."
verses.28:11: The woman asked, "Whom should I bring up for you?" And he answered, "Bring Samuel up for me."
verses.28:12: And the woman saw Samuel and cried out in a loud voice, and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, "Why did you deceive me, when you are Saul?"
verses.28:13: The king said to her, "Do not be afraid! What have you seen?" And the woman said to Saul, "I have seen a god coming up from the earth."
verses.28:14: He asked her, "What is his appearance?" And she answered, "An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe." Then Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
verses.28:15: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" And Saul answered, "I am in great distress, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and answers me no more, either through the prophets or by dreams. So I called for you to make known to me what I should do."
verses.28:16: Samuel said, "Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has departed from you and has become your adversary?
verses.28:17: The LORD has done for Himself just as He spoke through me; the LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.
verses.28:18: Because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD and did not execute His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has therefore done this thing to you this day.
verses.28:19: And the LORD will deliver Israel as well, along with you, into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The camp of Israel as well the LORD will deliver into the hand of the Philistines."
verses.28:20: At once Saul fell his full length to the ground and was greatly afraid because of the words of Samuel. There was also no strength in him, because he had not eaten bread all day and all night.
verses.28:21: Then the woman came to Saul and saw that he was deeply terrified, and she said to him, "Look, your maidservant listened to your voice; I put my life in my hand and listened to your words that you spoke to me.
verses.28:22: Now then, you also please listen to the voice of your maidservant, and let me place a piece of bread before you; eat, so that you may have strength when you go on your way."
verses.28:23: But he refused and said, "I will not eat." Yet his servants, and the woman as well, pressed him hard, so he listened to their voice. Then he got up from the ground and sat down on the bed.
verses.28:24: Now the woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it; then she took flour, kneaded it, and baked it into unleavened bread.
verses.28:25: She set it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate; then they got up and departed that night.
verses.29:1: Now the Philistines gathered all their camps to Aphek, while Israel was encamped by the spring that is in Jezreel.
verses.29:2: And the lords of the Philistines were passing along by hundreds and by thousands, while David and his men were passing along in the rear with Achish.
verses.29:3: Then the commanders of the Philistines said, "What are these Hebrews?" And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days or these years, and I have not found anything in him from the day he defected until this day?"
verses.29:4: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, "Send the man back, so that he may return to his place where you appointed him, and let him not go down with us into the battle, so that he does not become an adversary to us in the battle. For with what could this man reconcile himself to his master? Would it not be with the heads of those men?
verses.29:5: Is this not David, of whom they used to sing in the dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.29:6: Then Achish called David and said to him, "As the LORD lives, you are upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp is good in my eyes, for I have found no evil in you from the day of your coming to me until this day. Yet in the eyes of the lords you are not good.
verses.29:7: Now then, return and go in peace, so that you do not do what is evil in the eyes of the lords of the Philistines."
verses.29:8: And David said to Achish, "But what have I done, and what have you found in your servant from the day I have been before you until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
verses.29:9: Then Achish answered and said to David, "I know that you are good in my eyes, like an angel of God; nevertheless, the commanders of the Philistines have said, 'He must not go up with us into the battle.'
verses.29:10: So now rise early in the morning, with the servants of your master who came with you; rise early in the morning, and as soon as it is light for you, go."
verses.29:11: So David rose early, he and his men, to go in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.30:1: Now it happened when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had made a raid against the Negev and against Ziklag; they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
verses.30:2: And they had taken captive the women who were in it, from small to great; they had not put anyone to death, but had driven them off and gone on their way.
verses.30:3: And David and his men came to the city, and look, it was burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
verses.30:4: Then David and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.
verses.30:5: And David's two wives had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.30:6: And David was in great distress, for the people talked of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was bitter, each man over his sons and over his daughters. Yet David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
verses.30:7: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Please bring the ephod near to me." So Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.
verses.30:8: And David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Should I pursue this raiding band? Will I overtake it?" And He said to him, "Pursue, for you will certainly overtake and you will certainly rescue."
verses.30:9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Brook Besor, where those remaining behind stayed.
verses.30:10: And David pursued, he and four hundred men, while two hundred men stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross the Brook Besor.
verses.30:11: Now they found an Egyptian man in the field and took him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
verses.30:12: They also gave him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate, and his spirit returned to him; for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.30:13: Then David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" And he said, "I am an Egyptian young man, a slave of an Amalekite man; and my master abandoned me because I fell sick three days ago.
verses.30:14: We made a raid against the Negev of the Cherethites, and against what belongs to Judah, and against the Negev of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire."
verses.30:15: Then David said to him, "Will you bring me down to this raiding band?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will neither put me to death nor hand me over into the hand of my master, and I will bring you down to this raiding band."
verses.30:16: So he brought him down, and look, they were spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great plunder that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.30:17: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day, and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on the camels and fled.
verses.30:18: So David rescued all that Amalek had taken, and David rescued his two wives.
verses.30:19: And nothing of theirs was missing, from the small to the great, including sons and daughters, or from the plunder, even all that they had taken for themselves; David brought back everything.
verses.30:20: And David took all the flocks and the herds; they drove them ahead of that livestock and said, "This is David's plunder."
verses.30:21: Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David, whom they had left to stay at the Brook Besor; and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And David approached the people and asked about their welfare.
verses.30:22: Then every wicked and worthless man among the men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not go with me, we will not give them any of the plunder that we recovered, except to each man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away and go."
verses.30:23: But David said, "You must not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us; He has guarded us and has given the raiding band that came against us into our hand.
verses.30:24: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as is the share of the one who goes down into the battle, so will be the share of the one who stays by the baggage; they will share alike."
verses.30:25: And it came about from that day forward that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel until this day.
verses.30:26: When David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, "Here is a blessing for you from the plunder of the enemies of the LORD."
verses.30:27: To those in Bethel, and to those in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those in Jattir;
verses.30:28: and to those in Aroer, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa;
verses.30:29: and to those in Racal, and to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those in the cities of the Kenites;
verses.30:30: and to those in Hormah, and to those in Bor-ashan, and to those in Athach;
verses.30:31: and to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David had moved about, he and his men.
verses.31:1: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:2: And the Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
verses.31:3: The battle grew heavy against Saul, and the archers, men with the bow, found him; and he was in great anguish from the archers.
verses.31:4: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and pierce me with it, or else these uncircumcised men will come and pierce me and mistreat me." But his armor-bearer was not willing, because he was deeply afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.
verses.31:5: And his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he too fell on his sword and died with him.
verses.31:6: So Saul died, and his three sons and his armor-bearer, and all his men as well, together on that day.
verses.31:7: When the men of Israel who were across the valley and those who were across the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities and fled; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
verses.31:8: Now it happened on the next day that the Philistines came to strip the dead, and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:9: They cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent word all around the land of the Philistines to proclaim the good news in the house of their idols and to the people.
verses.31:10: They placed his armor in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
verses.31:11: Now the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard about him, what the Philistines had done to Saul.
verses.31:12: So all the valiant men arose and walked all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.
verses.31:13: Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

notes.1:5: Hebrew מָנָה אַחַת אַפָּיִם (lit. 'one portion of two faces/nostrils') is a difficult dual expression traditionally understood as a double or special portion.
notes.1:18: Hebrew וּפָנֶיהָ לֹא־הָיוּ־לָהּ עוֹד (lit. 'and her face was no longer to her') is an idiom meaning her distressed countenance was gone.
notes.1:24: The Masoretic Text reads בְּפָרִים שְׁלֹשָׁה ('with three bulls'), while v. 25 has the singular הַפָּר ('the bull'); in this verse the Septuagint and 4QSam-a reflect 'a three-year-old bull'.
notes.1:28: The Hiphil הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ ('I have lent him') and Qal passive participle שָׁאוּל ('lent') play on the root שׁאל ('ask') in vv. 20 and 27; the Masoretic text ends with singular וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ ('and he worshiped').
notes.2:3: Ketiv reads ולא ('and not'); Qere (translated here) reads וְלוֹ ('and by Him'), marking the agent of the Niphal verb נִתְכְּנוּ ('are weighed').
notes.2:16: Ketiv reads לו ('to him'); Qere (translated here) reads לֹא ('No').
notes.2:20: The Masoretic text has the 3ms Qal active שָׁאַל ('one asked', translated passively) rather than a 3fs verb, and the 3ms suffix לִמְקוֹמוֹ ('to his home/place').
notes.2:24: The clause מַעֲבִרִים עַם־יְהֹוָה is syntactically ambiguous: the Hiphil participle of עבר can mean 'passing along/circulating' with 'the people of the LORD' as subject, or 'causing to transgress' with Eli's sons as implied subject.
notes.2:32: Masoretic וְהִבַּטְתָּ צַר מָעוֹן is difficult: צַר with מָעוֹן ('dwelling', as in v. 29) may mean either 'distress in My dwelling' or 'a rival in My dwelling'; יֵיטִיב is an indefinite 3ms Hiphil ('what will be done for good').
notes.3:12: Hebrew closes with two infinitives absolute, the Hiphil of halal ("beginning") and the Piel of kalah ("finishing"), functioning adverbially to mean "from start to finish."
notes.3:13: The Masoretic Text reads "for themselves" (lahem), which Jewish tradition identifies as a scribal correction (tiqqun soferim) for "God" (reflected in the Septuagint). The Piel participle of qalal with this pronoun yields "calling a curse upon themselves."
notes.3:14: Hebrew uses the conditional particle im ("if") after the Niphal verb "I have sworn" as an emphatic negative oath ("will not"), followed by the Hithpael of kaphar in a passive sense ("be atoned for").
notes.4:8: Whereas 4:7 pairs Elohim ("God") with a singular verb ("has come"), the Philistines here combine Elohim with plural modifiers and a plural Hiphil participle ("these mighty gods... who struck"), reflecting their polytheistic view.
notes.4:13: The Ketiv reads yk (an apparent graphic error); the Qere yad (literally "hand," idiomatically "side," as in 4:18) is translated here as "beside."
notes.4:19: Hebrew uses the rare contracted Qal infinitive construct lalat (for standard laledet, "to give birth") and the Niphal of haphak (literally "turned upon her") for the sudden onset of labor pains.
notes.4:21: Ichabod means "Where is glory?" or "No glory." The Qal verb galah means "went into exile" or "departed," and "glory" (kavod) shares the same Hebrew root as Eli being "heavy" (kaved, 4:18) and the LORD's hand being "heavy" (5:6, 11).
notes.5:4: The Masoretic Text reads literally "only Dagon was left on him," referring to the remaining torso of the statue after its head and hands were severed; the Septuagint reads "the back/trunk of Dagon."
notes.5:6: Here and in 5:9, 12, the Ketiv reads opalim ("swellings/tumors") while the euphemistic Qere reads tehorim ("tumors/hemorrhoids"); the Qere is translated throughout.
notes.5:9: The verb "broke out" translates a Niphal hapax legomenon of the root satar (distinct from the homograph meaning "hide"), denoting an eruption of swellings.
notes.5:10: Here and in 5:11, the Masoretic Text uses collective first-person singular pronouns ("to me," "me and my people") for the speakers of Ekron as a community, whereas the Septuagint has the plural ("us," "our").
notes.6:4: For "tumors" (here and in 6:5), the ketiv uses opelim ("swellings/tumors") while the qere substitutes the euphemism tehorim ("tumors/hemorrhoids"). The Masoretic Text also reads "all of them" (3rd person plural suffix) before shifting to "your lords."
notes.6:6: Hebrew plays on the root kbd ("be heavy/honored") across 6:5-6—"give glory" (kabod) and "harden" (Piel, lit. "make heavy")—contrasted with the Hiphil of qll ("lighten") in 6:5.
notes.6:18: The Masoretic Text reads "as far as Great Abel" (lit. "the great meadow/watercourse"), whereas the parallel wording in 6:14-15 and some ancient versions read "the great stone" (eben instead of abel).
notes.6:19: The Masoretic Text juxtaposes "seventy men, fifty thousand men" without a conjunction, a celebrated numerical crux variously explained as "seventy men out of fifty thousand" or as a composite figure.
notes.7:2: The verb "lamented" translates a rare Niphal form of nhh (occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible), expressing mournful lamentation or earnest yearning in turning back toward the LORD.
notes.7:9: For "offered it up" (Hiphil of alah), the ketiv reads wy'lh without the final waw of the object suffix, while the qere vocalizes wayya'alehu with the explicit 3rd person masculine singular suffix.
notes.7:12: "Ebenezer" renders Hebrew Eben ha-Ezer ("Stone of Help"), playing on the verb "helped" (azar) in Samuel's words; "Shen" (ha-Shen) literally means "the Tooth" or "the Crag."
notes.7:16: Hebrew places the particle et before "all these places" as well as before "Israel," functioning either as an accusative of location or as the preposition "at/in."
notes.8:3: Hebrew contrasts two stems of the same verb (natah): Qal "turned aside" (after dishonest gain) and Hiphil "perverted" (lit. "bent aside" justice).
notes.8:9: "The practice of the king" (mishpat ha-melek, also in 8:11) uses the same Hebrew noun rendered "justice" in 8:3, here denoting the king's customary prerogative or manner of rule.
notes.8:15: "Officials" translates sarisim, royal court officers (at times eunuchs) serving the king's administration.
notes.8:16: The Masoretic Text reads "your finest young men" (bahurekem), whereas the Septuagint reflects "your cattle" (beqarekem).
notes.9:1: Ketiv reads מבן ימין ('from Ben-yamin', written as two words); Qere reads מִבִּנְיָמִין ('from Benjamin', one word). The phrase גִּבּוֹר חָיִל literally means 'mighty man of strength/substance,' denoting wealth and social standing in this context.
notes.9:17: Hebrew יַעְצֹר בְּ (Qal imperfect of עצר, literally 'restrain' or 'hold in check') is used idiomatically with the preposition בְּ to mean exercising governing authority over.
notes.9:21: Masoretic Hebrew reads שִׁבְטֵי בִנְיָמִן (plural construct, 'tribes of Benjamin'), likely referring to tribal subdivisions within Benjamin.
notes.9:24: Hebrew וְהֶעָלֶיהָ ('and what was on it') uses the definite article as a relative before a prepositional phrase. The clause לֵאמֹר הָעָם קָרָאתִי literally reads 'saying, "I have invited the people,"' indicating the time since Samuel announced the feast.
notes.9:26: Ketiv reads הגג ('the roof'); Qere reads הַגָּגָה ('to the roof', with directional he).
notes.10:5: 'Gibeah of God' literally translates 'the hill of God.' Hebrew נְצִבֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים uses the masculine plural construct ('garrisons' or 'outposts of the Philistines').
notes.10:7: Ketiv reads תבאינה; Qere reads the standard Qal imperfect 3fp form תָבֹאנָה ('they come'). The idiom 'whatever your hand finds to do' means to act as the occasion requires.
notes.10:19: Masoretic Hebrew reads וַתֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ ('and you have said to Him') followed by recitative or emphatic כִּי, rather than the variant 'No' (לֹא) reflected in some ancient versions.
notes.10:22: Masoretic Hebrew reads the indefinite אִישׁ ('a man') rather than 'the man,' and הֲבָא can be parsed as either Qal perfect ('has come') or Qal active participle ('is coming').
notes.11:6: Ketiv reads בשמעו ('at/in his hearing', with preposition בְּ); Qere reads כְּשׇׁמְעוֹ ('when he heard', with temporal preposition כְּ).
notes.11:9: Ketiv reads בחם ('in the heat of', with preposition בְּ); Qere reads כְּחֹם ('about the heat of,' i.e., 'by the time the sun is hot', with preposition כְּ).
notes.11:12: Hebrew שָׁאוּל יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ lacks an interrogative particle, expressing an incredulous rhetorical question by intonation ('Shall Saul reign over us?').
notes.12:5: Lit., 'and he said, "Witness."' The MT uses a singular verb here, understood collectively of the assembly of Israel speaking with one voice.
notes.12:10: Qere reads the plural 'and they said' (translated here), whereas ketiv writes the singular 'and he said,' taking Israel collectively.
notes.12:11: MT reads 'Bedan,' a deliverer not otherwise named in the book of Judges (some ancient versions read 'Barak').
notes.12:14: The final clause ('then both you and the king... will follow after the LORD') is rendered here as the result clause; some grammarians read it as continuing the conditional clause with an implied conclusion such as 'it will be well.'
notes.12:15: MT reads literally 'against you and against your fathers,' often understood elliptically as a comparison ('as against your fathers').
notes.13:8: Qere reads the Hiphil wayyiqtol 'and he waited,' whereas ketiv reflects a Piel or Niphal spelling of the same root; 'for the appointed time fixed by Samuel' renders an elliptical Hebrew phrase literally reading 'to the appointed time which Samuel.'
notes.13:15: MT moves directly from Samuel's ascent to Gibeah of Benjamin to Saul's muster of the six hundred men, without the longer narrative bridge found in the Septuagint.
notes.13:19: Qere reads the plural verb 'said' with 'the Philistines,' whereas ketiv writes the singular verb.
notes.13:20: MT lists two distinct agricultural tools derived from the Hebrew root meaning 'to plow' (translated 'plowshare' and 'plow-blade'), rather than 'sickle' as in some ancient versions.
notes.13:21: The rare noun rendered 'fee' denotes the sharpening charge, and a 'pim' is an ancient Hebrew weight attested on inscribed stones at about two-thirds of a shekel; 'a three-pronged fork' translates the Hebrew literally.
notes.14:14: Hebrew kebaḥăṣî maʿănāh ṣemed śādeh is literally "within about half a furrow of a yoke of field," referring to roughly half the furrow-length of the area a yoke of oxen could plow in a day.
notes.14:18: The Masoretic Text reads "the ark of God" (unlike the Septuagint's "the ephod") and closes with ûḇĕnê yiśrāʾēl, literally "and the sons of Israel," understood here as a comitative waw meaning "with the sons of Israel."
notes.14:27: Ketiv reads wtrʾnh ("and saw," from rʾh), while the translated Qere reads wattāʾōrnāh ("and brightened," Qal wayyiqtol from ʾwr), matching ʾōrû ("have brightened") in 14:29.
notes.14:32: Two Ketiv/Qere variants occur here: Ketiv wyʿś ("and did") against the translated Qere wayyaʿaṭ ("and pounced," Qal wayyiqtol from ʿyṭ), and Ketiv šll ("plunder") without the definite article against the translated Qere haššālāl ("the plunder").
notes.14:41: The Masoretic Text reads simply hāḇāh tāmîm, literally "give what is complete/true" (a true lot decision), without the longer Septuagint expansion mentioning Urim and Thummim.
notes.14:47: Hebrew yaršîaʿ (Hiphil imperfect of ršʿ, "condemn / declare guilty") is used here in the military sense of inflicting punishment or putting foes to the worse, whereas the Septuagint reads "he was saved."
notes.15:5: The verb translated "set an ambush" (wayyareb) is a defective Hiphil form of the root 'rb ("lie in ambush"), though identical in spelling to the Qal of ryb ("contend"); the noun nachal denotes a seasonal streambed or wadi.
notes.15:9: The plural noun translated "second-born" (hammishnim, literally "the second ones") is uncertain in meaning, likely referring to prime animals of the second birth or second year. The word translated "despised" (nemibzah) is an unusual passive participle form of the root bzh, paired with nāmēs (נָמֵס), a Niphal participle of the root mss ("melt, waste away"), translated "worthless."
notes.15:16: Ketiv reads "and they said" (wayyo'meru), whereas the Qere followed here reads the singular "and he said" (wayyo'mer), referring to Saul.
notes.15:29: The unique divine title translated "the Splendor of Israel" (netsach yisra'el) derives from a noun denoting eminence, splendor, enduringness, or everlastingness.
notes.15:32: The adverbial noun translated "confidently" (ma'adannot) is a lexical crux: derived from the root 'dn ("delight, ease"), it suggests walking cheerfully or at ease, though some link it by metathesis to 'nd ("in chains") or follow the Septuagint ("trembling").
notes.16:4: The Masoretic Hebrew verb "and said" (wayyo'mer) is third-person masculine singular (literally "and he said"), likely indicating an individual elder speaking on behalf of the group.
notes.16:7: The Masoretic clause "for it is not what a human sees" is intentionally elliptical (literally "for not what man sees"), without the explicit verb supplied in the Septuagint; likewise, "what meets the eyes" is literally "to the eyes" (la'enayim), contrasted with "to the heart" (lallebab).
notes.16:11: The verb "remains" (sha'ar) is the only Qal occurrence of this root in the Hebrew Bible (elsewhere Niphal or Hiphil). The verb "sit down" (nasob, Qal of sbb, "turn, surround") refers here to gathering around the table for the sacrificial meal.
notes.16:20: The concise Hebrew phrase translated "a donkey loaded with bread" is literally "a donkey of bread" (chamor lechem), an idiomatic expression for a donkey carrying a load of bread.
notes.17:4: The Hebrew phrase rendered 'champion' is literally 'the man of the space between,' referring to a warrior who fights single combat between opposing armies. The Masoretic Text gives his height as six cubits and a span, whereas the Septuagint and 4QSama read four cubits and a span.
notes.17:7: Following the Qere 'we-ets' ('and the wooden shaft of'), matching parallel descriptions in 2 Samuel 21:19 and 1 Chronicles 20:5; the Ketiv reads 'we-chets' ('and the arrow of').
notes.17:34: Hebrew uses singular verbs and habitual weqatal forms across verses 34-35 to describe repeated past encounters. The particle 'et' before 'the bear' is unusual before a subject and functions coordinately here ('or a bear').
notes.17:39: The verb rendered 'tried' is the Hiphil of 'ya'al' ('undertook, attempted'); the Septuagint appears to reflect a transposed root meaning 'grew weary' or 'struggled.'
notes.17:52: Masoretic Hebrew reads 'gay'' ('a valley,' or possibly a place name 'Gai'), whereas the Septuagint reads 'Gath,' matching the end of the verse.
notes.18:6: Following the Qere 'lashir' (Qal infinitive construct of 'shir,' 'to sing'); the Ketiv writes 'lshwr.' The rare noun 'shalishim,' derived from the root for 'three,' refers to a musical instrument such as a three-stringed lute or sistrum.
notes.18:9: Following the Qere 'oyen' (Qal active participle of the denominative verb from 'ayin,' 'eye'), meaning to watch with suspicion or jealousy; the Ketiv writes 'wn' defectively without the yod.
notes.18:14: The Hiphil participle 'maskil' (from 'sakal,' also in verse 15) denotes both wise, prudent conduct and the success that results from it.
notes.18:21: Hebrew 'bishtayim' (literally 'with two,' i.e., 'a second time') stands inside Saul's speech in the Masoretic Text, referring to a second opportunity to marry one of his daughters.
notes.18:29: Hebrew 'lero'' is a rare form of the Qal infinitive construct of 'yare'' ('to fear'), paired with the Hiphil of 'yasaf' ('added') and 'od' ('still/more') to express intensifying fear.
notes.19:9: The construct phrase ruach [divine name] ra'ah (lit. "a spirit of the LORD, evil") places the feminine adjective ra'ah ("evil") after the construct chain to modify ruach ("spirit"), indicating an evil spirit sent from the LORD. The Piel participle menaggen beyad literally means "playing music with the hand."
notes.19:13: The noun teraphim is plural in form, denoting here a human-sized household idol or image. The rare phrase kevir ha'izzim (occurring only here and in v. 16) refers to a woven covering, quilt, or cushion of goats' hair.
notes.19:18: Here and in 19:19, 22, 23 (and 20:1), the translation follows the Masoretic Qere reading Nayot ("Naioth"); the written Ketiv preserves a different consonantal spelling (nwyt in ch. 19; mnwwt in 20:1).
notes.19:20: The Qal verb wayyar ("and he saw") is masculine singular, used collectively or distributively of Saul's messengers. The noun lahaqat ("company" or "band") is a hapax legomenon, occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.20:2: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere lo-ya'aseh ("does not do," Qal imperfect); the written Ketiv reads lw 'sh ("did not do," spelling the negative lo as lw with the Qal perfect). The idiom "disclosing it to me" is literally "uncovering my ear" (also in vv. 12-13).
notes.20:12: The verse opens with an elliptical oath invocation (lit. "The LORD, the God of Israel"), and its closing negative clause connects directly to the self-imprecation at the beginning of v. 13 ("may the LORD do so to Jonathan...").
notes.20:14: The Masoretic Hebrew of this verse is highly compressed, using welo ("and not") three times: the opening rhetorical negative question is paused by the condition "if I am still alive," resumed before "show the faithful love of the LORD," and followed by the purpose/result clause "so that I do not die."
notes.20:19: The Piel verb shillashta (denominative from shalosh, "three") means "do on the third day," followed by tered me'od (lit. "go down greatly/quickly"). Both "the day of the deed" (yom hamma'aseh) and "the stone Ezel" (ha'even ha'azel) follow the Masoretic text directly.
notes.20:38: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere plural hachitzim ("the arrows"); the written Ketiv has the singular hachetzi ("the arrow"), matching the singular in vv. 36-37. In 20:24, the Qere reads the preposition el ("to") where the Ketiv reads al.
notes.21:3: The verb translated "I have directed" is an unusual Poel (or variant Hiphil) form of the root yd' ("know"), occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible with the sense of appointing or directing someone to a place.
notes.21:6: The idiom translated "as before" literally means "as yesterday and the day before," which may also mean "for about three days" since David set out. The final clause ("will it be holy in the vessel") is terse; "vessels" (keli) may refer to the young men's gear or euphemistically to their bodies.
notes.21:9: The Masoretic Text has the unusual form ve'in (pointed with hireq) before yesh ("there is"), functioning as an interrogative ("Is there not...?") equivalent to ha'en.
notes.21:14: The verb "he changed" (Piel of shnh) carries a proleptic third-person masculine singular object suffix anticipating "his demeanor." The verb "he scratched marks" (Piel of tvh) follows the Masoretic Hebrew rather than the Septuagint's "drummed."
notes.22:3: The Masoretic Text reads a Qal jussive of ytza ("come out") with "with you," a pregnant construction meaning "come out and be with you."
notes.22:14: The phrase "who turns to your bidding" translates the Masoretic Hebrew Qal participle of sur ("turn aside") with mishma'at ("obedience, bidding"), referring to attentive compliance with the king's orders.
notes.22:17: Qere reads "my ear" (ozni), fitting Saul's first-person speech; ketiv has "his ear" (ozno).
notes.22:18: Here and in 22:22, the qere spells the name "Doeg" with aleph (do'eg), whereas the ketiv spells it with yod (doyeg).
notes.22:22: The verb "I myself have brought this upon" translates sabbothi (Qal perfect of sbb, "turn around" or "bring about"), used uniquely here in the sense of being the cause or occasion of the disaster.
notes.23:6: The Masoretic Text makes "an ephod" the grammatical subject of the Qal perfect verb yarad ("came down"), literally "an ephod came down in his hand."
notes.23:7: The verb "has handed him over" translates nikkar (Piel perfect of nkr, "treat as foreign" or "alienate"), used here in the sense of delivering someone into another's hand.
notes.23:9: The participle translated "plotting" (maharish) is a Hiphil participle of hrsh ("plow, engrave, devise"), which elsewhere carries the sense "devise" or "plot" in the Qal stem.
notes.23:15: Horesh (hachorshah, with the definite article and -ah ending) is either a place name in the wilderness of Ziph or a common noun meaning "wooded region" or "thicket."
notes.23:28: Hebrew Sela-hammahlekoth, literally "the Rock of the Divisions" (from hlq, "divide," referring to the parting of Saul and David, or possibly "the Rock of Slipping Away/Escape" from the homonymous root meaning "be smooth").
notes.24:4: Hebrew literally reads "to cover his feet" (Hiphil infinitive construct of sakak), an idiom and euphemism for relieving oneself.
notes.24:5: The qere reads singular "your enemy," matching the following singular pronoun "to him," whereas the ketiv reads plural "your enemies."
notes.24:8: The verb "checked" renders the Piel of shasa', which literally means "to tear apart" or "to cleave," used here metaphorically for sharply restraining his men with words.
notes.24:11: Hebrew "Someone said" uses an indefinite third-person masculine singular verb, and "my eye spared you" translates the feminine singular verb wattahos (Qal wayyiqtol of hus) with its standard implied feminine subject "eye."
notes.24:16: Hebrew literally reads "judge me from your hand" (Qal imperfect of shaphat with min), a forensic idiom meaning to vindicate or deliver by rendering judgment.
notes.25:3: The qere reads "a Calebite" (a descendant of Caleb), whereas the ketiv consonants suggest kelibbo ("according to his own heart," i.e., self-willed) or a wordplay on "dog" (keleb).
notes.25:6: Hebrew koh lehai (literally "thus to life" or "to the living one") is an idiomatic greeting wishing long life and prosperity.
notes.25:14: The verb "lashed out" translates the Qal of 'it, literally "to swoop down upon" like a bird of prey, used figuratively here for raging at David's messengers.
notes.25:22: The Masoretic Text explicitly reads "to the enemies of David" as a euphemistic self-curse formula, and "one who urinates against a wall" (also in 25:34) is a blunt Hebrew idiom for any male.
notes.25:25: Hebrew plays on Nabal's name (nabal, meaning "fool") and the cognate noun "folly" (nebalah).
notes.26:16: The phrase "deserve to die" translates the Hebrew idiom literally "sons of death," denoting those liable to capital punishment.
notes.26:19: "May He smell an offering" renders the Hiphil jussive of the verb meaning "to smell," the biblical cultic idiom for God accepting a sacrifice.
notes.26:22: The qere reads "the king's spear" in standard construct form without an article on "spear," whereas the ketiv prefixes the definite article to the construct noun.
notes.26:23: The Masoretic Text literally reads "into hand" without a possessive suffix, understood from context as "into my hand."
notes.26:25: "Surely act" and "surely prevail" render two paired Qal infinitive absolute constructions, the first using the verb "do/act" absolutely in the sense of acting effectively.
notes.27:4: The qere reads the Qal perfect ("he did not continue"), whereas the ketiv reflects an imperfect form with the same sense.
notes.27:7: "A year" renders Hebrew yamim, literally "days," a standard biblical idiom for a full annual cycle.
notes.27:8: The qere reads "the Gizrites" (associated with Gezer), whereas the ketiv reads "the Girzites."
notes.27:10: The Masoretic Text has the negative particle al before a perfect verb, an unusual construction translated here as a negative question ("Did you not make a raid?"), whereas ancient versions reflect "Where" or "Against whom did you raid?"
notes.28:7: "A woman who is a medium" renders Hebrew eshet ba'alat-ov, literally "a woman, mistress of a spirit of the dead"; in v. 8, the same noun ov refers to divining by such a spirit.
notes.28:8: The qere reads the Qal feminine singular imperative "divine" (qasomi), whereas the ketiv writes a plene spelling with waw (qswmy) reflecting the o-vowel.
notes.28:13: "A god" renders Hebrew elohim, here denoting a spirit or shade rising from the underworld; it takes the plural participle "coming up" in grammatical concord even though v. 14 describes a single figure.
notes.28:16: "Your adversary" translates the rare Hebrew noun ar ("enemy, adversary") attested in the Masoretic Text.
notes.28:17: The Masoretic Text reads "for Himself" (lo), referring reflexively to the LORD, whereas the Septuagint and Vulgate read "to you."
notes.29:2: Hebrew sarne (lords) is the distinctive Philistine title for their city-state rulers, in contrast to sare (commanders, vv. 3, 4, 9), the Hebrew term for military officers or officials.
notes.29:3: Hebrew noflo (Qal infinitive construct of nafal, 'to fall') literally means 'his falling,' used idiomatically in military contexts for defecting to another side.
notes.29:4: Hebrew yitratseh (Hithpael imperfect of ratsah, 'to be pleased with') literally means 'make himself acceptable' or 'reconcile himself.'
notes.30:10: Hebrew piggeru (Piel perfect of pagar) occurs only here and in v. 21 in the Hebrew Bible and denotes being too faint or exhausted to go on.
notes.30:13: Hebrew hayyom sheloshah literally reads 'today three,' an idiomatic expression meaning 'three days ago.'
notes.30:17: Hebrew neshef denotes twilight (either dusk or dawn), and lemochoratam literally reads 'to their next day,' an unusual suffixed form meaning 'of the next day.'
notes.30:20: The asyndetic Hebrew clause nahagu lifne hammiqneh hahu ('they drove [them] ahead of that livestock') refers to the newly captured Amalekite herds being driven in front of the recaptured Ziklag livestock.
notes.30:22: The Hebrew shifts from singular immi ('with me'), reflecting the speech of each individual objector, to plural nitten ('we will give') and hitsalnu ('we recovered').
notes.31:3: Masoretic vayyachel is pointed as a Qal wayyiqtol of chil/chul ('to writhe, be in anguish'); ancient versions often rendered it 'was wounded' as if from chalal ('to pierce, wound').
notes.31:9: Hebrew levasser (Piel infinitive construct of basar) means 'to proclaim good news'; bet atsabehem ('house of their idols') stands parallel to et-ha'am ('the people') and may be understood as either 'in the house of their idols' or 'to the house of their idols.'
notes.31:11: Hebrew elav ('about him' or 'concerning it') is proleptic, anticipating the following object clause 'what the Philistines had done to Saul.'
